Here's the full picture, now with precise numbers across the actual named badge categories (Runway, Campaign, Exclusive, Online Exclusive, VIC Exclusive — the five names that show up together in SFCC-225/132's own comments):

**How it breaks down, measured live in the browser at the real mobile card width (179px):**

| Badge name | Clearance before the close button |
|---|---|
| Runway | 35.8px to spare |
| Campaign | 23.3px to spare |
| Exclusive | 28.4px to spare |
| VIC Exclusive | 7.7px to spare — tight, but fine |
| **Online Exclusive** | **overlaps by 15.8px** |

That's a meaningfully different risk profile than my first pass suggested — worth knowing precisely rather than just "long text is risky."

**Why it happens:** the badge and the close button are both positioned independently and unconditionally — `badge` is `position: absolute; left: 0` and sizes itself to whatever text it's given (no max-width, no truncation), while `close` is `position: absolute; right: 0` at a fixed 48px. Neither one knows the other exists. There's no collision-avoidance logic between them anywhere in the recipe, and nothing scales down for mobile — the same fixed 24px/20px insets apply at every card size (confirmed earlier this session, straight from Figma). So on a wide-enough card the gap between them is huge and it's a non-issue; on the actual 179px mobile card, that gap gets thin enough for the longest real badge name to eat through it.

**Why only Wishlist:** it's the only variation with both a badge *and* a close button sharing that same top row. PLP has a badge but no close button there — nothing to collide with. Home has neither.

**How I tested it:** I forced the rendered card's container down to 179px — the actual mobile pixel width confirmed against Figma, not a guess — and read real `getBoundingClientRect()` values off the live DOM, not the Storybook canvas's own fixed-320px decorator. That's a faithful test, not a synthetic one: the badge/close positioning has zero responsive/breakpoint CSS on it (confirmed — no media query touches either one), so shrinking the container reproduces exactly what a real mobile viewport would render.

**Why I didn't just fix it:** every option involves guessing at a visual treatment nothing has specified — truncate with an ellipsis, wrap to two lines, drop to a smaller badge font on mobile, or something else. Figma's own reference never pictured anything longer than the placeholder "LABEL," so there's no design to be faithful to here, only ones to propose.

content.text:
Confirmed precisely — you're right, and I can show exactly why.

**Measured:** the badge text's vertical center sits **9px lower** than the close icon's vertical center. Root cause: badge wrapper height = **64px**, close button height = **48px** — they're not the same box height, so centering each one's own content independently puts them at different heights.

**Why Figma doesn't have this problem:** Figma's "Tag" frame is a **fixed 48px-tall frame** — exactly matching Close's 48px — with the text centered inside that fixed height via symmetric internal spacing (12px + 8px = 20px above the text, 20px below, 48px total either way). Close's icon is centered the same way, in its own fixed 48px frame. Same fixed height, same centering logic on both sides → they land on the same horizontal line automatically.

**What my code actually does differently:** when I built the badge, I deliberately collapsed Figma's real `Tag → touchContainer → Label` nesting into one wrapper, reasoning that the `touchContainer` level only existed for a tap-target that a static text label doesn't need — which is a fine call on its own. But I implemented that wrapper with **padding only, no fixed height** (`paddingBlock: 20px`, no `height`). Padding-only sizing means the wrapper grows to fit *padding + content* — 20 + content + 20 = 64px measured, not the fixed 48px Figma actually uses. So it's not that the two are centered differently — it's that they're each centered within a *different total height*, and only one of the two boxes (Close's) is actually the height Figma specifies.

**The fix:** give the badge wrapper the same fixed `height: var(--zimm-scale-1200)` (48px) that `close` already uses, add `display: flex; align-items: center` to center the text within that fixed height, and drop `paddingBlock` (no longer doing anything once the height is fixed and centering is flex-driven) — keeping only the horizontal `paddingInline`. Same fixed-box-with-centered-content pattern Close already uses, just applied consistently to both.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNPreBuild

The gate before code. Nothing gets built until every source has been checked and every gap has
been named.

**Intended model: Opus 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — set it
yourself before invoking. The plan synthesis step delegates to the `zm-planner` agent, which is
pinned to Opus regardless of the session model, so the expensive judgement runs on Opus either
way.

**Input:** `SFCC-83 and SFCC-84 (Recently Viewed UI Component + Recently Viewed See Full History), being folded into the existing feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component branch. Context: SFCC-236's ZimmProductCard organism is already built, audited and committed (10 commits, local only, no PR yet) but has zero real consumers — SFCC-83/84 are being picked up specifically to wire it up. Both are assigned to Marcel, both "In Progress", both directly Jira-blocked by SFCC-236. SFCC-84's card behaviour is confirmed to reuse the existing 'plp' variation; SFCC-83's rail is confirmed to exclude both the badge and the hover model-photo swap per Dani Rivett's scope note.` — a Jira key (e.g. `SFCC-194`), optionally followed by a depth.
If no key is given, ask for one before doing anything else.

## Depth

Depth is a parameter, not an adverb. Pick one and say which you are using:

| Depth | Jira + Confluence | Codebase | Figma |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quick` | the ticket and its direct links | branch state, file tiers | the named node only |
| `standard` *(default)* | ticket, links, comments; targeted Confluence search | tiers, blast radius, nearest existing pattern | node, variants, states |
| `exhaustive` | full link graph, all comments, related epics, all matching Confluence | above, plus every consumer of every touched file and the exemplar PR diffs | node, all variants, all states, all viewports, token mapping |

Never substitute a stronger adverb for a depth. "In-depth full-on exhaustive" is not a level;
`exhaustive` is.

---

## Phase 0 — position

Call `/session-start`. It confirms the branch, reads the tracking docs, runs health checks and
states current position.

Then confirm one thing it does not: **you cannot be on `develop` or `main`.** A `PreToolUse` hook
blocks every Write and Edit on those branches, so a plan handed to the builder from `develop` is
dead on arrival. If the branch is wrong, say so and stop — do not create a branch unasked.

---

## Phase 1 — gather

Run these **in parallel**. Each one ends in its own findings block. Never let a clean source hide
a broken one — report all five, even when four are fine.

### Jira — `mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue`

Pull the story and read all of it: description, requirements, acceptance criteria, linked design,
attachments, linked work items, and the full comment thread. Comments routinely carry the
decision that contradicts the description.

Flag: missing or untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments ·
no linked design · attachments referenced in prose but not attached · linked work items that are
still open and block this one · a decision made in comments that never made it into the description.

### Confluence — `confluence_search`, `confluence_get_page`

Search for anything bearing on this story: TSDs, integration docs, data dictionaries, decisions.

Flag: no TSD where the work clearly needs one · a TSD that contradicts the ticket · documentation
describing an approach the codebase does not implement · a page last updated before a decision
that supersedes it.

### FED handbook — `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md`

The build approach: tokens, components, CSS structure, overriding, accessibility, tests, stories.
Part I is the machine, Part II the procedure, Part III the role.

Flag: handbook guidance that contradicts what the codebase now does · a claim whose cited
`file:line` no longer resolves · anything the story needs that the handbook does not cover.

The handbook is a derived account, not the source. **Where it disagrees with
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`, that file wins** — and say so, because it means the handbook
is stale.

### Codebase

Branch state, and the shape of what is about to be touched.

- Confirm `develop` is current with `origin/develop`.
- For every likely-touched file: tier and owner, from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and
  `protectedFiles.md`. **Never from `.claude/registry/*.md`** — its Tier column is a derived
  heuristic and is wrong in places.
- Call `/audit-tier <path>` for anything you are unsure about. It also returns import blast radius.
- Find the nearest existing pattern. This codebase has strong precedent; matching it is cheaper
  and more reviewable than inventing.
- Read the exemplar PRs when the story touches their surface: **PR #64** (ui-kit atom/molecule,
  four-file pattern, co-located recipe, render-slot wiring), **PR #59** (global-chrome component,
  co-located recipe with shared cross-file values), **PR #56** (pure token layer, no component
  change).

Flag: any Tier 1 file in the likely set · high blast radius (a shared file with many consumers) ·
work that crosses squad territory · an existing pattern the story would contradict.

### Figma

- Design System 2026 — `https://www.figma.com/design/wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm/Zimmermann_Design_System_2026`
- Zimmermann_Designs — `https://www.figma.com/design/QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs/Zimmermann_Designs`

**Ask for one node URL per variant and per state**, not one per component. If the file-level
links are not enough to resolve the specific component, stop and ask Marcel. Do not guess at
which node the story means, and do not build from a neighbouring node that looks close.

Check:

- **Completeness** — every variant and every state: hover, focus, active, disabled, loading,
  error, empty, success.
- **Currency** — is this design archived or superseded? Triage archived against current before
  anyone builds to it. An archived node that still renders is a trap.
- **Tokenisation** — does every value map to an existing `--zimm-*` token, or is a new token
  being introduced? A new token is Tier 1 and needs the designer.
- **Responsiveness** — frames exist at 402 / 1023 / 1440; breakpoint tokens are 768 / 860 / 1024.
  **The 768–1022 band is unframed**, so anything in it is an inference, not a design.

Two measurement traps that have produced false defects here. Flag a comparison that hits either:

- **Node type decides comparability.** Figma TEXT nodes report a cap-height box, which is not
  comparable to a CSS line box — never file a mismatch from one. FRAMES and INSTANCES report a
  real box and are directly comparable.
- **The two Figma files must never be cross-compared.** The Design System file and the Designs
  file are different sources; a delta between them is not a defect.

**No design is a blocker, not licence to invent.** If the ACs name something Figma does not have,
that is a finding for Marcel — or an explicit **provisional**, labelled as such and carried into
the plan as an assumption. Never fill the gap silently.

Flag: missing variants or states · a design that is archived or superseded · values with no token
· the unframed tablet band left to inference · a design that contradicts an established component
· no design at all where the story implies one.

---

## Phase 2 — reuse

These already exist. Call them; do not reimplement them.

1. `/feature-spec` — turns the gathered picture into a scoped implementation plan and emits a
   ready-to-paste scoped prompt.
2. `/scope-check` — run it **on that prompt**. It verdicts SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED and rewrites
   risky prompts. This is the highest-leverage gate available; do not skip it.
3. `/audit-tier <path>` — per file, wherever scope-check flags something specific.

Two known traps when calling these:

- `/code-quality` defaults to diffing against **`main`**; `/pr-checklist` diffs against
  **`develop`**. On a feature branch these give different file sets. Always pass explicit scope.
- `/pr-checklist` already calls `/code-quality` internally. Calling both doubles the audit.

None of these skills emits machine-readable output — they all return prose for a human. If you
need to branch on a result, restate the verdict yourself rather than parsing theirs.

---

## Phase 3 — the gate

This is the part that earns the skill. Produce one table, every source, every gap:

| # | Source | Finding | Severity | What unblocks it |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Severity is one of:

- 🔴 **BLOCKED** — cannot plan around it. A missing AC, an absent design, a Tier 1 file with no
  owner approval, a `scope-check` BLOCKED verdict. **Stop here.** Report and wait for Marcel.
- 🟡 **CLARIFY** — plannable, but the plan carries a stated assumption. Name the assumption
  explicitly in the plan so it is visible if it turns out wrong.
- 🔵 **NOTE** — worth knowing, does not affect the plan.

**Do not fill a gap with an assumption and carry on silently.** A missing acceptance criterion is
a finding, not something to infer. The whole point of the gate is that it stops.

---

## Phase 4 — plan

Delegate to the `zm-planner` agent (Opus). Give it everything gathered — all five findings blocks,
the `/feature-spec` output, and the `/scope-check` verdict.

It returns: goal statement · scale call (multi-commit or multi-branch, with reasoning) · file
manifest with tiers and owners · steps with concrete pass criteria · per-step loop configuration ·
open questions.

Write the result to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`, and write the Phase 3 gate
table to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/findings.md`.

Create the run directory if it does not exist. **Never write run state into the repo.**

---

## Phase 5 — handoff

Present to Marcel, in **"ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead"** register — not dumbed down, but without
jargon that gets in the way. Lead with the consequence, then the mechanism, then the fix.

1. The gate table — blockers first.
2. The plan summary — scale call, step count, file count with tier breakdown.
3. Every stated assumption, gathered in one place.
4. The paths to `plan.md` and `findings.md`.

Then say plainly whether this is ready for `zimmerMANNBuild`, or what is blocking it.

**Put decisions to him one at a time, using AskUserQuestion.** Do not present a wall of choices
and do not bundle unrelated calls into one question.

**This skill stops here. It never invokes `zimmerMANNBuild`** — Marcel does, once he has read the
gate. Discover → report → wait for approval → and execution is a separate, deliberate act.

**Do not hand off with an unresolved 🔴.** Handing a blocked plan to the builder is how a
build burns an afternoon on the wrong thing.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never modify anything.** This skill reads, checks and plans. The only files it writes are

1	*This document is for documenting what has been learned - What worked, what failed, what NOT to do again.*
2	
3	## SFCC-751 QA automation pipeline (2026-08-24/25)
4	
5	- **Test locally before pushing anything that triggers real CI, especially BrowserStack** — it
6	  costs real session quota. When debugging a CI failure, reproduce it locally first rather than
7	  keep iterating against a live PR. Confirmed developer preference — redirected mid-session after
8	  a live-PR debugging detour: "I wanted to test this via the CLI BEFORE we push to Git and it
9	  runs its tests."
10	- **`browserstack-node-sdk` requires its config file literally named `browserstack.yml`, no
11	  leading dot.** A `.browserstack.yml` is silently never found — every SDK-driven run fails at
12	  config resolution before any test executes. This repo had the dotted name since it was first
13	  created and never caught it, because no PR had ever gotten `e2e-browserstack` far enough to hit
14	  that step successfully before SFCC-751's first real run (PR #61).
15	- **BrowserStack Test Observability groups results by test *title* across Playwright projects,
16	  not by project.** Two tests sharing an identical title (the same `test()` running under both
17	  `chromium` and `mobile-chrome`) collapse to one dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded*
18	  status — confirmed via the real API, not just the dashboard UI (a build with 11 real chromium
19	  passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles reported `passed: 0,
20	  skipped: 11`). `test.skip()` does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and
21	  still clobbers. Real fix: genuinely separate spec files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/`
22	  folders, which `playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already routes
23	  correctly (`chromium` ignores `**/mobile/**`, `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`) — not a
24	  same-file/distinct-title workaround, which still gets the "wrong" project's test collected (and
25	  skipped) regardless of its title.
26	- **Jira Cloud's "Sprint" field has no stable API alias.** It's `customfield_10020` on this
27	  instance specifically (confirmed live via a real field search) — an instance-specific ID, not
28	  safe to assume unchanged on a different Jira site.
29	- **BrowserStack's Test Observability API strips the leading `@` from Playwright tags.** A spec's
30	  own `@zephyr:KEY` tag comes back as `zephyr:KEY` (no `@`) in the `Get Tests` API response —
31	  easy to get wrong since the source `.spec.js` file's tags do have `@`.
32	- **Chakra modal close animations aren't instant.** A consent-dismiss helper that clicks decline
33	  and returns immediately can hand control back while the dialog is still mid-fade-out and
34	  technically "visible" — a caller that immediately checks for a *different* dialog right after
35	  can match both and get a Playwright strict-mode "resolved to 2 elements" error. Wait for
36	  `state: 'hidden'` after the click, not just for the click to register.
37

- **Test locally before pushing anything that triggers real CI, especially BrowserStack** — it
  costs real session quota. When debugging a CI failure, reproduce it locally first rather than
  keep iterating against a live PR. Confirmed developer preference — redirected mid-session after
  a live-PR debugging detour: "I wanted to test this via the CLI BEFORE we push to Git and it
  runs its tests."
- **`browserstack-node-sdk` requires its config file literally named `browserstack.yml`, no
  leading dot.** A `.browserstack.yml` is silently never found — every SDK-driven run fails at
  config resolution before any test executes. This repo had the dotted name since it was first
  created and never caught it, because no PR had ever gotten `e2e-browserstack` far enough to hit
  that step successfully before SFCC-751's first real run (PR #61).
- **BrowserStack Test Observability groups results by test *title* across Playwright projects,
  not by project.** Two tests sharing an identical title (the same `test()` running under both
  `chromium` and `mobile-chrome`) collapse to one dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded*
  status — confirmed via the real API, not just the dashboard UI (a build with 11 real chromium
  passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles reported `passed: 0,
  skipped: 11`). `test.skip()` does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and
  still clobbers. Real fix: genuinely separate spec files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/`
  folders, which `playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already routes
  correctly (`chromium` ignores `**/mobile/**`, `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`) — not a
  same-file/distinct-title workaround, which still gets the "wrong" project's test collected (and
  skipped) regardless of its title.
- **Jira Cloud's "Sprint" field has no stable API alias.** It's `customfield_10020` on this
  instance specifically (confirmed live via a real field search) — an instance-specific ID, not
  safe to assume unchanged on a different Jira site.
- **BrowserStack's Test Observability API strips the leading `@` from Playwright tags.** A spec's
  own `@zephyr:KEY` tag comes back as `zephyr:KEY` (no `@`) in the `Get Tests` API response —
  easy to get wrong since the source `.spec.js` file's tags do have `@`.
- **Chakra modal close animations aren't instant.** A consent-dismiss helper that clicks decline
  and returns immediately can hand control back while the dialog is still mid-fade-out and
  technically "visible" — a caller that immediately checks for a *different* dialog right after
  can match both and get a Playwright strict-mode "resolved to 2 elements" error. Wait for

  (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.

      "value": "What we need to finalise user stories per epic
----------------------------------------------

PWA Kit user stories cannot be written, reviewed or signed off until the relevant design components are locked. Here is what that means in practice.

### 1 — Components must be finalised first

* Before user stories can be written for an epic e.g. Checkout Flow & Delivery, **every UI component that appears in that epic must be finalised in the UI kit** — fully componentised in Figma with all variations, states and responsive sizes accounted for. This allows us to build the component user story.
* Each component is owned by the **earliest epic in the sequence where it appears**. That epic is responsible for designing all variations of that component — including any variations needed by later epics. For example, if a product card component appears on PDP, PLP and Homepage, all three variations must be designed and locked as part of the PDP.

> As we move through the epic sequence, design effort should reduce. By the time we reach epics like Homepage or Wishlist, most components should already exist. Design at that stage should be limited to anything genuinely net-new.

### 2 — Design freeze

* **Hard rule:** Once a component is finalised and added to the UI kit, **it is locked — no further UX or design changes are permitted**. User stories are written against locked designs only. Any change after lock requires a formal review of every story and epic that references that component.

### 3 — Sign-off checklist per epic

* Before component user stories are submitted for PO review, confirm the component has ALL variations included in the UI kit.

## The gate: **BLOCKED**. No build plan produced — I deliberately didn't invoke the planner.

The headline: **SFCC-83 is close to plannable. SFCC-84 is a much bigger job than its ticket suggests**, and its ticket has no acceptance criteria at all.

### What actually blocks this

**1. SFCC-84 has no ACs.** Its entire description is *"This is a follow-up user story for the page behind the 'See Full History' link."* That's it. Nothing on fields, pagination, item cap, empty state, or auth behaviour.

**2. SFCC-84's design needs two components that don't exist — and one isn't even its job.** The page mockup is `Navigation + Logo masthead + `**`PLP Bar desktop`**` + 4 × Products Module + Footer`. Each module is 4 × **`Products S Desktop` at 288×542** — that's *taller* than `ZimmProductCard` (288×432), so it's a different component, not a variation of the card you just built. And a PLP filter/sort bar belongs to the PLP epic, not to "a page behind a link."

**3. The rail is a Product Card Group — and SFCC-743's contract can't express it.** The Figma decomposes as `title-and-link` + `group` of **5** `Product-card`s. That's literally SFCC-743's prop contract (`showTitleAndLink`/`showLink`/`title`/`linkLabel`), and SFCC-118 explicitly says recommendation rails render via SFCC-743. But 743's `display` only supports **3, 4, 6** — so 5 doesn't fit, which is now the *second* count it can't express (PLP's 36 being the first). SFCC-743 is also Blocked, and neither 83 nor 84 links to it.

**4. PLP scope is a straight contradiction.** `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (Confirmed): *"do not implement on those surfaces until confirmed"* — naming PLP. SFCC-83's AC: *"Confirmed surfaces are PLP, PDP, and Cart."* Per AGENTS.md doc-integrity the PRD wins, so the ticket is the thing that needs fixing.

**5. The storage mechanism is invented, not specified.** SFCC-83 promises history *"available on login from any device"* — cross-device, so server-side. PRD-027 (Confirmed) says only *"browsing session history"* and specifies no store at all. The repo has **zero** storage code and **zero** customer-attribute writes. Today's rail is Einstein `viewed-recently-einstein` — and Einstein zone setup (SFCC-112) is Blocked and doesn't even list Recently Viewed.

**6. Consent gating lives in a Blocked ticket.** SFCC-106 holds a real AC — *guest without consent → no rail at all* — and is blocked pending the Tell No Lies / Vicky Routley review.

### Good news, for the record

Your designs are real and better than the trackers suggested: the rail has **all three viewports including a Tablet frame at 768** — a band the handbook records as unframed and inference-only everywhere else. The card geometry (288×432) matches `ZimmProductCard` exactly. And the "thumbnail only, no name or price" line in the PRD turns out to describe *current Magento*, not the new design — so that scare is dead.

Two smaller things: node `8802:10232` doesn't resolve (deleted, or the URL got clipped), and ~40 of the ~50 nodes are still unmapped — no hover/focus/**empty state** located yet for either story, and states are AC-level.

## Correction block — retracts #1, #3, #22 (raised by Marcel, verified)

### Retraction 1 — SFCC-84 *does* have acceptance criteria. Finding #1 is withdrawn.

**Mechanism of the error:** ACs on this Jira instance live in **`customfield_10231`** ("Acceptance Criteria",
project-scoped ADF textarea). `jira_get_issue` returns `description` and `comments` but **not** that field.
Every ticket read in this run — and in the earlier SFCC-236 audit — was read without it. SFCC-236 was only
covered by luck: Jasmijn had pasted its updated ACs into comment 13891, so they arrived via a side channel.

**Fix for future runs:** always pull `customfield_10231` explicitly, e.g.
`jira_search` with `fields=summary,customfield_10231`.

SFCC-84's real ACs: See-Full-History link appears when items exceed the visible rail width · each tile
renders **consistently with PLP tile behaviour (as per SFCC-80)** · **total item count displayed top-right
of the page** · clicking a tile navigates to PDP.

### Retraction 2 — neither "missing component" is missing. Finding #22 is withdrawn.

- **`Products S Desktop`** (288×542) — opened the node: `Solid` image block 288×**440** + `info` block
  288×**92** containing product name, price, and a hidden 20×20 `Icons` slot. That is the *same*
  image-block + info-block shape as `ZimmProductCard`, whose real card heights are 489 / 522 / 546. 542 sits
  inside that family. **Two errors compounded:** I compared 542 against **432**, which is the card's *image*
  height not its *card* height; and I compared a `Zimmermann_Designs` node against a `Design_System_2026`
  node, which this skill explicitly forbids ("a delta between them is not a defect").
- **`PLP Bar desktop`** (1440×75) — opened the node: it contains only `Recently Viewed Container` →
  `Recently Viewed Text` (left) + `Full History Text` (59px, right-aligned at x=1159). It is a **title row,
  not filter/sort chrome.** I inferred filter chrome from the component's *name*. The right-aligned element
  maps exactly onto SFCC-84's AC 3 (item count, top right).

Both corrections stand. Taking them in order:

## The ACs — I was reading the wrong surface

They live in **`customfield_10231`** ("Acceptance Criteria"). `jira_get_issue` returns `description` and `comments` but **not** that field. So every ticket I've read this whole session was read without it — including the SFCC-236 audit a few hours ago, where I only had the ACs by luck because Jasmijn had pasted them into comment 13891. That's not method, that's an accident. Fixed going forward: pull `fields=customfield_10231` explicitly.

Having now read them properly, they're *better* than the descriptions suggested — and SFCC-236's AC block has a dedicated **"Recently Viewed Full History variation (same behavior as PLP card)"** section with five ACs. So SFCC-236 already formally covers SFCC-84's card. That's real alignment, not a gap.

## The "two missing components" — neither is missing

**`Products S Desktop`** — I opened the node this time. It's `Solid` image block 288×**440** + `info` block 288×**92** carrying product name, price and a hidden 20×20 icon slot. That's the same image-block + info-block shape as `ZimmProductCard`, whose actual card heights are 489/522/546. 542 sits inside that family. I made two mistakes at once: I compared 542 against **432**, which is the card's *image* height not its card height — and I compared a `Zimmermann_Designs` node against a `Design_System_2026` node, which this skill explicitly forbids ("a delta between them is not a defect").

**`PLP Bar desktop`** — despite the name, it contains only `Recently Viewed Text` (left) and `Full History Text` (59px, right-aligned at x=1159). It's a **title row, not filter chrome.** I inferred a filter bar from the component's name without opening it. And that right-aligned element is precisely SFCC-84's AC 3 — *"the total number of recently viewed items is displayed in the top right."*

## The pattern, since this is the third time today

Badge/close "overlap" — I compared padded boxes instead of visible ink. `Products S Desktop` — a bounding-box number instead of the node's children. `PLP Bar desktop` — a name instead of its contents. The ACs — a tool's default fields instead of the ticket's real fields. Same shape every time: **reasoning from a proxy instead of opening the thing.** You caught all four by looking at the actual artefact.

## What survives

Four blockers, and the ACs sharpened two of them rather than clearing them:

- **Storage mechanism** — now explicit in AC 7: *"when they log in on **any device**, then their history is restored."* Cross-device is an acceptance criterion, and no source names a mechanism. Repo has zero storage code and zero customer-attribute writes.
- **PLP scope** — AC 9 says *"embedded on PLP, PDP and anywhere else"*; `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 says don't implement on PLP until confirmed.
- **SFCC-743** — its own AC 6 covers only *"size=Desktop or size=Mobile"*, but this rail has a **Tablet** frame at 768. So 743 can express neither the 5-card count nor the Tablet viewport.
- **Consent** — SFCC-83's AC 6 duplicates SFCC-106's guest AC nearly verbatim, and SFCC-106 is Blocked.

Also new: AC 5 says the See-Full-History link appears when items *"exceed the visible rail width"*; Confluence 04.2 says *"visible if there's more than one product."* Two different trigger rules.

This function pulls together event user parameters for both the write and read paths, attaching the SLAS session cookie ID plus, if registered, the encrypted user ID.

This is huge: it means AC 7 is achievable natively through Einstein with no custom storage needed. When authenticated, both the view-activity write and recommendations read carry the stable encrypted customer ID, so Einstein ties browsing history to the actual customer across devices; for guests, only the session-scoped cookie ID is sent, matching AC 6's session-clearing requirement exactly. So the base SDK already implements the guest-vs-authenticated split that SFCC-83 describes -- the "unspecified storage mechanism" concern may not actually be a blocker since the mechanism already exists.

But I still need to be careful about what's genuinely open: Einstein isn't configured for Zimmermann (it points at the Salesforce demo org), so SFCC-112's zone/provisioning work remains Blocked -- though I should note that "Recently Viewed" is a recommender, not a zone, and SFCC-112's scope explicitly covers Recommended-for-You and More-from-Category zones, not Recently Viewed, so this may be a smaller ask than SFCC-112's full scope. There's also the policy constraint against enabling Einstein on SIT, which limits testing, and I need to verify that Einstein's userId actually delivers the cross-device restoration AC 7 requires in practice, not just in principle.

This also sharpens the consent question in SFCC-106 -- since Recently Viewed would be Einstein-backed, it's genuinely a third-party personalization call that belongs on SFCC-106's consent-gated list, strengthening that finding. And critically, if Recently Viewed really is Einstein-backed, SFCC-83 shrinks dramatically: there's no custom storage layer to build, just a rail component wired to the existing recommendations hook.

Before finalizing, I want to verify one more thing responsibly: whether `isRegistered` and `getEncUserIdWhenReady` are genuinely wired into a registered-customer path in this repo, and whether SLAS tokens actually expose a `usid`/`encUserId`. ## Storage-mechanism investigation (2026-09-04) — downgrades #4 from 🔴 to 🟡

Marcel's recollection was right: it is Einstein, and it is already live.

### Established from code

- **Live today on the PDP:** `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1120` renders base
  `RecommendedProducts` with `recommender={EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED}` =
  `'viewed-recently-einstein'`, inside `<Island hydrateOn='visible'>`.
- **Write path:** `einstein.sendViewProduct(product)` → `POST /activities/{siteId}/viewProduct`.
- **Read path:** `getRecommendations(name)` → `POST /personalization/recs/{siteId}/{name}`.
- **Both paths append the same identifier pair** (`use-einstein.js:522-527`, applied on every activity
  and on `getRecommendations` at `:581-589`):

  ```js
  const getEventUserParameters = async () => ({
      cookieId: await getUsidWhenReady(),                                 // SLAS usid — session/device
      userId: isRegistered ? await getEncUserIdWhenReady() : undefined    // encrypted customer id
  })
  ```

  resolved from `useUsid()`, `useEncUserId()` and `useCustomerType()` (`:447-449`).

**Consequence:** the base SDK already implements exactly the guest-vs-authenticated split the ACs
describe. Guests send only a device/session `cookieId` → history is device-scoped and dies with the
session (**AC 6**). Authenticated shoppers additionally send a stable encrypted `userId` → history is
keyed to the customer, not the device (**AC 7**'s "on any device"). **No custom storage layer needs
designing, and nothing needs persisting to a `c_*` customer attribute.**

**This also dissolves the PRD-vs-AC tension** inside #4: PRD-027's "browsing *session* history" and
AC 7's cross-device restore are not contradictory — Einstein does both, selected by auth state.

### What Marcel saw in development was demo-org data

- `.env.sample:96` → `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID=aaij-MobileFirst` — Salesforce's **reference/demo** site ID.
- `config/default.js:143` → `einsteinId: '1ea06c6e-c936-4324-bcf0-fada93f83bb1'` — the SDK's demo ID,
  hardcoded (Tier 1 file, read-only here).

So the working Recently Viewed rail was returning **Salesforce demo catalogue** recommendations, not
Zimmermann's. It proves the *plumbing* works; it proves nothing about Zimmermann's own data.

### Honest residuals — why this is 🟡 and not cleared

1. **Vendor behaviour unverified.** The `userId` is present on both calls, but whether the
   `viewed-recently` **recommender** actually returns cross-device history for an authenticated user is
   Einstein-side behaviour that cannot be established from this codebase. Needs Salesforce doc
   confirmation or a live test against a provisioned org.
2. **Zimmermann's Einstein is not provisioned.** But the dependency is **narrower than first recorded**:
   SFCC-112's scope is creating named **zones**, and its zone list covers Recommended-for-You and
   More-from-Category — *not* Recently Viewed. `viewed-recently-einstein` is a **recommender**, not a
   zone, so this likely needs only Einstein *enabled*, not SFCC-112's zone work. Confirm with Bianca.
3. **Einstein is policy-barred on SIT** (project policy, not code-enforced), which constrains where this
   can be demoed and tested.

### Knock-on: #6 (consent) is strengthened, not weakened

If the data source is Einstein, Recently Viewed **is** a third-party personalisation call — and SFCC-106
lists *"Einstein Recommendations — Analytics"* in its own consent-gating scope. So consent gating is
structural to this feature, not incidental, and SFCC-106 being Blocked matters more, not less.

### Revised shape of SFCC-83

Remaining work collapses to: build the rail (Product-Card-Group-shaped, composing `ZimmProductCard`) and
wire it to the existing `useEinstein().getRecommendations('viewed-recently-einstein')`. Note base
`RecommendedProducts` already owns that fetch **but renders base `ProductTile`** — so the fetch logic must
either be re-homed into a Zimmermann container or `recommended-products/` must be overridden (Tier 2,
Squad B, copy-first). That is the same architecture fork as #5/#21.

| # | Revised |
|---|---|
| 4 | 🔴 → 🟡 **CLARIFY.** Mechanism exists and is wired; no custom storage to build. Open: vendor cross-device behaviour, and Zimmermann provisioning (narrower than SFCC-112). |
| 6 | 🔴 **Stands, stronger.** Einstein is explicitly on SFCC-106's consent-gated list. |

So it proves the plumbing works; it proves nothing about Zimmermann's own data.

**Two honest residuals, which is why I've moved this to 🟡 rather than cleared it:**

1. The `userId` is present on both calls, but whether the `viewed-recently` **recommender** actually returns cross-device history is Einstein-side behaviour I can't establish from code. Needs Salesforce docs or a live test against a provisioned org.
2. So this likely needs only Einstein enabled, not SFCC-112's zone work — worth confirming with Bianca.

**One thing got worse, not better:** if the data source is Einstein, then Recently Viewed *is* a third-party personalisation call — and SFCC-106 lists "Einstein Recommendations — Analytics" in its own consent-gating scope. So consent is structural to this feature, not incidental, and SFCC-106 being Blocked now matters more.

**And SFCC-83 shrinks a lot.** Remaining work: build the rail (Product-Card-Group-shaped, composing `ZimmProductCard`) and wire it to the existing `useEinstein().getRecommendations('viewed-recently-einstein')`. The catch: base `RecommendedProducts` already owns that fetch but renders base `ProductTile` — so either the fetch moves into a Zimmermann container, or `recommended-products/` gets overridden (Tier 2, Squad B, copy-first). content.text:
That corroborates it exactly — the feature "switching on" with the API key is the signature of pure base-SDK plumbing. Nothing custom was ever built; a valid Einstein credential was the only missing piece.

## Is SFCC-743 in scope for 83/84?

**No — not formally, and not yours.** It's a separate story, assigned to **Kiera**, labelled Squad-A, status **Blocked**, with its own 10 ACs. And I verified the link graph from both sides: 743 is blocked-by SFCC-236 and blocks SFCC-80/118/314. It has **no link to SFCC-83 or SFCC-84**, and neither of your stories links to it.

But architecturally it's the same object. The Recently Viewed rail decomposes in Figma as `title-and-link` + `group` of `Product-card`s — which is 743's description almost word for word ("renders an optional section header (title + link) and a responsive row of ProductCard components"). And SFCC-118, the sibling carousel story, states outright that it *"renders using the Product Card Group component (SFCC-743)."* So the precedent for a rail on this project is: go through 743.

The catch — and this is the concrete answer rather than a philosophical one: **even if you took 743 in today, it couldn't render this rail as designed.** Its `display` prop supports 3, 4, 6 — the Recently Viewed Desktop rail shows **5**. And its AC 6 covers only `size=Desktop or size=Mobile` — this rail has a confirmed **Tablet** variant at 768. So 743's contract would need widening on two axes before it could serve SFCC-83.

## Is this mainly UI?

**Mostly — but the ticket does say otherwise, and it's worth knowing where.** SFCC-83's ACs include four that aren't presentational:

- AC 2 — tiles ordered most-recently-viewed first
- AC 6 — guest: session-scoped, cleared when the session ends
- AC 7 — authenticated: restored on login, on any device
- AC 8 — empty state: component not rendered at all

Notably, SFCC-83 has **no scoping sentence**. Compare SFCC-236, which explicitly says *"The component is scoped to the visual and interactive layer only — product data is sourced from SFCC."* SFCC-83 carries no equivalent, so it's broader than 236 by omission rather than by design.

The saving grace is what we just established: Einstein already returns the list recency-ordered, already scopes guests by `cookieId`, and already keys authenticated shoppers by `userId`. So ACs 2/6/7 are **data-shaped ACs that the base plumbing already satisfies** — meaning the actual build is UI-dominant with thin wiring, even though the ACs aren't UI-only. AC 8 is genuinely yours (render nothing when empty).

SFCC-84 is more straightforwardly UI: tile-per-PLP, item count top-right, click→PDP, plus the link-availability rule.

Holding off on the blockers as you said. I'll fold whatever you decide on 743 and the scope boundary into the gate file when you get there.

content.thinking:
Marcel's pushback is fair, so I want to take it seriously rather than dismiss it. Looking back at the mockup structure, the sidebar is built from a Products Module Desktop block that itself contains four smaller Products S Desktop components arranged together, which is exactly the kind of nesting that makes "just stacked rows" feel like an oversimplification.

Now I need to actually check whether that structure repeats identically across the whole sidebar — four Products Module Desktop instances stacked vertically, each holding four cards side by side, ending in a Footer. If so, Marcel's right that it's literally rows in Figma, but the real question for him is whether calling it a "grid" versus "stacked rows" changes anything meaningful for implementation, since the visual outcome — a 4×4 layout — looks identical either way even though the underlying container logic and behavior could differ.

The critical distinction is that stacked rows would mean chunking product data into groups of four in JavaScript, which breaks down at different breakpoints and creates accessibility issues since screen readers would announce separate row containers instead of one list. A CSS grid, by contrast, lets one container with sixteen children reflow naturally without JS intervention, stays semantically correct as a single list, and matches how PLP grids are conventionally built. Figma shows discrete rows simply because it lacks a native concept of wrapping content into as many rows as fit — that's a tooling limitation, not evidence for how the code should actually be structured.

But I want to double check myself: is there any case where grouping into real rows would be legitimate, like if each row represented a distinct category with its own heading (say, "Today" vs "Yesterday")? I need to check whether the module's metadata shows any such heading before ruling that out entirely.

content.text:
**Yes — you're right, it's literally stacked rows in Figma.** Four `Products Module Desktop` instances stacked vertically, each holding 4 cards side by side. I called it a grid because that's what it *should be built as*, and I skipped the step of saying why. Let me do that properly.

## The ELI5

They look **identical** on screen. 4 rows × 4 cards = 16 cards in a 4-column arrangement. You could not tell from a screenshot which way it was built.

The difference is *who decides where the wrapping happens.*

**Built as stacked rows:** you take the list of products and chop it into groups of four in JavaScript, then render one row component per group. The "4 per row" number lives in your code.

**Built as a grid:** you hand CSS all 16 cards in one container and say "columns of 288px, wrap as needed." CSS decides where rows break.

Why that matters: on mobile you want 2 across, not 4. With a grid, that's one CSS line and it just reflows. With stacked rows, your JS chopped the array into fours *before* CSS ever saw it — so at mobile you'd get rows of 4 squeezed, or you'd have to re-chop the array per breakpoint. **JavaScript can't see breakpoints the way CSS can**, so you end up duplicating layout logic in the wrong layer. That's the whole argument.

There's a second reason: a screen reader announces stacked rows as four separate containers, versus one list of sixteen products. The grid is the honest structure.

## Why Figma shows rows regardless

Figma has no "wrap into as many rows as fit" primitive. A designer placing 16 cards *has* to draw discrete rows, and repeating one module instance four times is the tidy way to do it. So **stacked-rows-in-Figma is a drawing artefact, not a specification** — the same class of thing as `PLP Bar desktop` being named like a filter bar when it's actually a title row. The file records how it was drawn, not how it should be built.

## I did check whether the rows are real

If each row had its own heading — "Today", "Yesterday", "Last week" — then the rows would be *semantically* real and stacked rows would be correct. They don't. Each `Products Module Desktop` contains exactly four cards and **nothing else**: no text node, no heading, no editorial insert. The rows are homogeneous and interchangeable, which is the tell that they're a grid drawn as rows.

For what it's worth, the geometry is a clean 4-across full-bleed: cards at x = 0, 384, 768, 1152, each 288 wide → 96px gaps, totalling exactly 1440. (Provisional numbers, so don't hold me to them.)

One smell worth noting: the `Footer` instance inside that same `Sidebar` frame is also exactly 1440×606 — the same height as a products module. A real footer wouldn't happen to be exactly one module tall. That's consistent with the mockup being rough, which is presumably why you marked the file provisional.

**All three ruled out:**

1. **SFCC-81 "PLP UI - Hero & (Sub Category) Links"** — this "hero" is a full-width category banner at the top of a PLP (Tall/Medium/None depending on category level: Collections/Category/Sub-category). Not a product card at all.

Both are visually **ordinary small product tiles** — badge top-left, product image, name below. No enlarged image, no spanning layout, no visual "featured" treatment of any kind. Nothing about it looks like a hero.

**Conclusion: "Hero" in the Product-card component set and "Hero" in SFCC-81/218/882 are two unrelated uses of the same word.** One is a page-level banner (real, ticketed, three tickets deep). The other is a `Size` variant value sitting alongside `Desktop`/`Mobile` inside the Product-card component — and it has **no owning ticket anywhere in this Jira project.** That's consistent with everything found earlier: only 2 instances (every real variation has 6+), no Hover, no Unavailable, and small internal inconsistencies between the two copies that suggest an abandoned duplicate rather than a finished variant.

My guess was wrong — only one tile is visible, stacked vertically with the start of another below it, confirming the Flex row is actually constrained to the meta's 320px width rather than laying tiles out side by side.

So the flex container's wrapping is governed by its own computed width, not by overflow behavior — I was conflating two different mechanics. Since the parent Box sets width to 320px, and two 288px tiles plus a 24px gap exceed that, flexWrap:'wrap' correctly wraps the tiles onto separate lines regardless of overflow settings.

This means I do need to override the decorator at the story level with a wider container to get the layout I want, adding a story-specific decorators array that provides a much wider Box or removes the width constraint entirely.

Since Storybook doesn't seem to offer a clean way to opt out of meta-level decorators per story, I should stop fighting the composition and instead let the gallery's own layout handle overflow explicitly rather than relying on flexWrap to avoid it.

Since MemoryRouter doesn't add its own DOM wrapper and Chakra's Box has no overflow set by default, switching to nowrap should let the tiles sit side by side and overflow visibly rather than clipping. I'll change flexWrap from "wrap" to "nowrap" in the galleryRow helper, or just drop it since Flex defaults to row+nowrap anyway.

Let me apply this edit and take another screenshot to confirm it works.

## Confirmed working end to end

`nodeCoverage/` is now correctly visible to git (`??`, untracked but trackable — no longer silently swallowed by the `coverage` ignore pattern), Storybook indexes it clean with no ID collisions, and the full suite is still 860/860.

Live-verified in the browser, not just assumed:
- Sidebar shows a proper **Commerce → ZimmProductCard → Coverage** folder, sibling to the 8 original stories, each of the 19 entries individually named with its Figma node ID right in the sidebar label
- Spot-checked one entry from each row — `Home_Desktop_Default` (renders, correct args), `PLP_Mobile_Unavailable` (badge + name correct; notify-me text absent is expected — desktop hover-gating still applies since this is a width-only mobile simulation, exactly as the file's own documented limitation says), `Wishlist_Desktop_Default` (badge, attributes, price all correct), and the **Hero placeholder** (renders its exclusion message and both node IDs, no error)

**What's at `nodeCoverage/index.stories.tsx`:**
- 18 stories, one per real Figma node (Home/PLP/Wishlist × Desktop/Mobile × Default/Unavailable), each independently named and clickable, each citing its exact node ID in both the sidebar name and its own docblock
- 1 `Hero_ExcludedNotInScope` story — kept as a real, visible entry rather than omitted, so the folder's count (19) versus the Figma file's count (20) is self-explanatory instead of looking like a missed node

Two mistakes caught and fixed along the way, worth having on record: the `coverage` folder name collided with this repo's own `.eslintignore`/`.gitignore` convention for generated test-coverage reports — the file existed on disk but was invisible to git entirely until renamed to `nodeCoverage`. And Storybook's own dev-server process cached the old path in memory after the rename, needing a real restart (not just a browser refresh) to clear.

Not committed. Given the shape of this change — retiring the gallery approach from `index.stories.tsx` and adding this new folder — want it as one commit, or should the removal and the addition be separate?

1	# SFCC-236 — Product Card Shared Component: Build Plan
2	
3	**Generated:** 2026-09-02 · **Planner:** `zm-planner` (Opus) · **Gate:** [findings.md](./findings.md)
4	**STATUS: GATE PASSED — ready for `zimmerMANNBuild`.** All blocking questions resolved; Tier 2 crossing approved
5	by Marcel 2026-09-02. Branch not yet cut (skill rule: never create a branch unasked).
6	**Scope: SFCC-236 only.** SFCC-83 and SFCC-84 are held — blocked on data source, surface list, and Legal's consent ruling.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 1. Goal
11	
12	Build the shared Zimmermann Product Card per SFCC-236 (8 pts, Sprint 4, epic SFCC-2), designed in Figma
13	`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` set `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size × State × Type × Unavailable), following the
14	FED handbook's ui-kits atomic layering and the PR #64 / `zimmColourSwatchGroup` pattern — named-export
15	component reading a `Zimm*`-namespaced multipart recipe via `useMultiStyleConfig`, parts applied with
16	`<chakra.div __css={styles.x}>`, all values `var(--zimm-*)` with explicit media queries.
17	
18	**The card is the visual layer only:** every value arrives as a prop, it owns no data fetching, and it renders
19	the add-to-bag / size-selection controls without wiring their behaviour (SFCC-185 / SFCC-497 / SFCC-90).
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 2. Scale call — one branch, seven commits, one PR
24	
25	```bash
26	git fetch origin && git checkout -b feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component origin/develop
27	```
28	
29	The current checkout (`feature/SFCC-91_...`) is merged and must not be built on.
30	
31	**Why one branch despite ~24 files:** one component family, one Figma set, one ticket, one reviewer set
32	(`pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` on every file). The molecules have exactly one consumer — the organism — so
33	merging them separately merges dead code. Splitting would also multiply the single Tier 2 touch
34	(`theme/components/index.ts`) across three approval cycles for an append-only registry edit.
35	
36	**Full build loop (Implementer → Tester → Scorer per step).** This is a keystone blocking eight tickets, so a
37	wrong prop contract propagates into eight downstream stories.
38	
39	### Deliberately dropped
40	
41	| Dropped | Why |
42	|---|---|
43	| Copy-first | Nothing to copy — no file is being overridden at a mirrored path |
44	| Playwright / `.feature` | No page renders this component on this branch; E2E belongs to SFCC-80/90/497 |
45	| Bundle-size / LCP step | Nothing imports the card yet; bundle delta is zero |
46	| Visual regression | Chromatic/Loki is out of budget (`testing.md` excludes it); hover fidelity is a manual Storybook check |
47	| Multi-region fixtures | The card takes pre-formatted strings; no locale/currency logic to vary |
48	
49	**Retained, non-negotiable:** `npx tsc --noEmit` · `npm run test` · `npm run lint` · `npm run audit:tokens` ·
50	`cr review --light --base develop`.
51	
52	---
53	
54	## 3. File manifest
55	
56	### Modified (3)
57	
58	| File | Tier | Owner |
59	|---|---|---|
60	| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | **Tier 2** | `tier-2-approvers` + `tier-1-approvers` (CODEOWNERS:117) |
61	| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.tsx` | 3/4 | `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` |
62	| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice/index.test.tsx` | 3/4 | same |
63	
64	**The Tier 2 file is the only tier crossing.** AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 → needs explicit scope confirmation
65	before Step 1. No Tier 1 file is touched.
66	
67	### Created (21) — all Tier 3/4, `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b`
68	
69	Root `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/`, each with `index.tsx` · `index.stories.tsx` · `index.test.tsx` · `<name>.css.ts`:
70	
71	```
72	molecules/zimmSlideIndicator/
73	atoms/zimmSizeChip/
74	molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/
75	molecules/zimmProductCardMedia/
76	molecules/zimmProductCardContent/
77	organisms/zimmProductCard/          + zimmProductCardShared.ts
78	```
79	
80	**Explicitly NOT created: `overrides/app/components/product-tile/`** — creating it activates the resolver for
81	PLP, Search, Home, Cart, PDP and empty-search-results, and `product-list/index.jsx:51-53` imports
82	`{Skeleton as ProductTileSkeleton}`, so an override without that named export breaks PLP at import time.
83	
84	`zimmProductCardShared.ts` holds DOM-contract constants (`data-card-slot` names) + `CARD_BP` derived from
85	`theme/foundation/gridSystem`. No design values, so it stays co-located (precedent:
86	`zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`). Keeps the Tier 2 surface at exactly one file.
87	
88	---
89	
90	## 4. Architecture decisions
91	
92	**Variation axis = discriminated union (data contract) + declarative config table (layout).**
93	`typescript.md` mandates the union, and the ACs require it: Wishlist alone needs `colour` + `size` + mandatory
94	`onRemove`; PLP alone needs `sizes` + `onNotifyMe`. A flat optional-everything bag lets you build a Wishlist
95	card with no remove CTA (AC violation) and a PLP card with one (design violation).
96	
97	```
98	ZimmProductCardProps = Base & (PlpVariation | HomeVariation | WishlistVariation)
99	  base:       id, href, name, headingLevel, primaryImage, hoverImage?, images?,
100	              currentPrice?, originalPrice?, isUnavailable?, badge?
101	  'plp':      sizes?, selectedSize?, onSizeSelect?, onAddToBag?, onNotifyMe?
102	  'home':     —
103	  'wishlist': colour, size, onRemove (required), onAddToBag?
104	```
105	
106	`'recently-viewed'` is **not** a fourth member — the AC says it behaves identically to PLP, so consumers pass
107	`variation: 'plp'`. Recorded as an assumption, not a silent choice.
108	
109	The render body must **not** `switch` on `props.variation`. Layout comes from a module-level `VARIATION_CONFIG`
110	(`showBag`, `showAttributes`, `showRemove`, `hoverHidesPrice`, `hoverRevealsPrice`, `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`,
111	`hoverSwapsImage`). That is what satisfies the extensibility AC: add a union member + a config row, touch no JSX.
112	
113	**The card is fluid, not 288px.** `gridSystem.ts` has `maxWidth: 'none'`. Figma's 288/179 are widths at the
114	reference artboards. The card fills its grid cell (`width: 100%`); the image holds ratio via `aspectRatio`.
115	Grid placement belongs to SFCC-80.
116	
117	**Mobile/desktop boundary = 768px** (`breakpoints.md`, 48em) — the only confirmed foundation breakpoint between
118	the 402 and 1440 artboards, and where the grid already goes 4→8 columns. `min-width` is inclusive, so the 768
119	artboard gets the desktop card. Every hover rule is additionally gated on `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`
120	so a 768px touch tablet never gets hover-only content. See OQ-5.
121	
122	**Hover is CSS-only, keyed on `:hover, :focus-within`.** No React hover state — 60 tiles re-rendering on pointer
123	move is a PLP perf defect. `:focus-within` is not optional: WCAG 2.2 AA requires the revealed size selector and
124	arrows be keyboard-reachable. All reveal selectors live in one place, the organism's recipe root part, selecting
125	descendants by the shared `data-card-slot` constants. Molecules stay hover-agnostic.
126	
127	**One link per card (stretched-link).** The card holds a bag button, arrows, size options and a remove button —
128	nesting those in an `<a>` is invalid HTML and an a11y failure. The link wraps the product name only and carries
129	a `::after { position:absolute; inset:0 }` overlay; controls get `position:relative; z-index:1`. `href` arrives
130	pre-prefixed from the page. Uses `import {Link as RouteLink} from 'react-router-dom'` per `zimmColourSwatch` —
131	there is no `overrides/app/components/link/` override, contrary to a claim in `overrideStyling.md`.
132	
133	**Reuse, don't rebuild:** `ZimmProductName`, `ZimmProductPrice`, `ZimmIcon` (`bag`, `close`, `chevron-left`,
134	`chevron-right` all exist in `ICON_MAP`). No new icons.
135	
136	**VIC pricing is not a card concern** — precedence is the page mapper's job. Deferred to SFCC-778 (OQ-6).
137	
138	---
139	
140	## 4a. Arrows vs. indicator — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)
141	
142	> *"position indicator is just for tablet and mobile, desktop hover is arrows"*
143	
144	The two are **mutually exclusive**, not paired. Consequences for Steps 1 and 4:
145	
146	**Split by pointer capability, not viewport width.** The gate is
147	`@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` — the same gate every other hover rule already uses:
148	
149	- **hover-capable + fine pointer** → prev/next arrow buttons, revealed on `:hover, :focus-within`. No indicator.
150	- **everything else (touch tablet, mobile)** → `ZimmSlideIndicator`, always visible. No arrows.
151	
152	Capability rather than width is what actually delivers the stated intent: the 768 artboard is a *touch* tablet,
153	and a width rule alone would give it arrows it can never hover to reveal. It also keeps this consistent with the
154	card's own hover rules rather than introducing a second, differently-keyed breakpoint. **Edge case, accepted:**
155	a desktop browser resized below 768 keeps arrows (it still has a fine pointer); a touch-screen laptop gets the
156	indicator. Both are the safe failure direction — nobody is shown a control they cannot operate.
157	
158	**Two knock-on changes to the step pass criteria:**
159	
160	1. **Step 1 — the indicator is NOT `aria-hidden` on touch.** The original criterion assumed the arrow buttons
161	   announce position, so the indicator could be hidden as duplicate. Where the indicator renders there are **no
162	   arrows**, so it becomes the only position signal — hiding it would be a 1.1.1 information loss. It needs an
163	   accessible position announcement (e.g. a visually-hidden "Image 3 of 8" live region, or `role="group"` with
164	   `aria-label`). Revised criterion: exposed and announced when it is the sole affordance.
165	2. **Step 4 — mobile image paging has no mechanism and no AC.** If the indicator shows position on touch, some
166	   touch gesture must change the image. No AC covers this; the ACs only describe desktop hover. See OQ-11.
167	
168	---
169	
170	## 4b. Touch image paging — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)
171	
172	> *"scroll-snap it is"*
173	
174	Native CSS scroll-snap. The dots remain a **passive readout**, visually unchanged from Figma — no enlargement,
175	no conversion to tap targets, so no departure from the design and no WCAG 2.5.8 problem to solve.
176	
177	**Implementation shape: one scroll container on every breakpoint, not two mechanisms.**
178	
179	The image strip is always a horizontally scrollable flex container with `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` and
180	`scrollSnapAlign: 'start'` on each slide. What differs by pointer capability is only the *affordance* layered
181	over it:
182	
183	| | Mechanism | Affordance |
184	|---|---|---|
185	| hover + fine pointer | same scroll container | arrows call `scrollBy()`; no indicator |
186	| touch | same scroll container | native drag; indicator reflects position |
187	
188	One container rather than two code paths means a single source of truth for "which image is showing", the
189	arrows become progressive enhancement over something that already works, and the desktop path inherits
190	keyboard scrollability for free.
191	
192	**Active-index derivation:** prefer `IntersectionObserver` on the slides over a scroll listener — 60 tiles on a
193	PLP make a per-scroll-event listener a real perf cost, and the repo already has
194	`overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.ts` (**Tier 2 — import it, do not modify it**). The `scrollend`
195	event is an acceptable alternative. Left to the Implementer; either satisfies the pass criteria.
196	
197	**Precedent:** the base `ProductScroller`
198	(`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller/index.jsx:79-84`) already uses
199	`scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` with `overflowX: 'scroll'`. Same technique, already proven in this codebase.
200	
201	**Accepted caveat:** swipe has no explicit affordance beyond the dots implying further content. This is the
202	universal mobile convention, and the alternative (enlarging 1px dots into 24×24 tap targets) trades an
203	invisible-but-expected gesture for a visible-but-off-design control. **Action: flag to Kiera that the mobile

# SFCC-236 — Product Card Shared Component: Build Plan

**Generated:** 2026-09-02 · **Planner:** `zm-planner` (Opus) · **Gate:** [findings.md](./findings.md)
**STATUS: GATE PASSED — ready for `zimmerMANNBuild`.** All blocking questions resolved; Tier 2 crossing approved
by Marcel 2026-09-02. Branch not yet cut (skill rule: never create a branch unasked).
**Scope: SFCC-236 only.** SFCC-83 and SFCC-84 are held — blocked on data source, surface list, and Legal's consent ruling.

---

## 1. Goal

Build the shared Zimmermann Product Card per SFCC-236 (8 pts, Sprint 4, epic SFCC-2), designed in Figma
`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` set `40000223:2822` (20 variants: Size × State × Type × Unavailable), following the
FED handbook's ui-kits atomic layering and the PR #64 / `zimmColourSwatchGroup` pattern — named-export
component reading a `Zimm*`-namespaced multipart recipe via `useMultiStyleConfig`, parts applied with
`<chakra.div __css={styles.x}>`, all values `var(--zimm-*)` with explicit media queries.

**The card is the visual layer only:** every value arrives as a prop, it owns no data fetching, and it renders
the add-to-bag / size-selection controls without wiring their behaviour (SFCC-185 / SFCC-497 / SFCC-90).

---

## 2. Scale call — one branch, seven commits, one PR

```bash
git fetch origin && git checkout -b feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component origin/develop

## 4. Architecture decisions

**Variation axis = discriminated union (data contract) + declarative config table (layout).**
`typescript.md` mandates the union, and the ACs require it: Wishlist alone needs `colour` + `size` + mandatory
`onRemove`; PLP alone needs `sizes` + `onNotifyMe`. A flat optional-everything bag lets you build a Wishlist
card with no remove CTA (AC violation) and a PLP card with one (design violation).

```
ZimmProductCardProps = Base & (PlpVariation | HomeVariation | WishlistVariation)
  base:       id, href, name, headingLevel, primaryImage, hoverImage?, images?,
              currentPrice?, originalPrice?, isUnavailable?, badge?
  'plp':      sizes?, selectedSize?, onSizeSelect?, onAddToBag?, onNotifyMe?
  'home':     —
  'wishlist': colour, size, onRemove (required), onAddToBag?
```

`'recently-viewed'` is **not** a fourth member — the AC says it behaves identically to PLP, so consumers pass
`variation: 'plp'`. Recorded as an assumption, not a silent choice.

The render body must **not** `switch` on `props.variation`. Layout comes from a module-level `VARIATION_CONFIG`
(`showBag`, `showAttributes`, `showRemove`, `hoverHidesPrice`, `hoverRevealsPrice`, `hoverRevealsSizeSelector`,
`hoverSwapsImage`). That is what satisfies the extensibility AC: add a union member + a config row, touch no JSX.

**The card is fluid, not 288px.** `gridSystem.ts` has `maxWidth: 'none'`. Figma's 288/179 are widths at the
reference artboards. The card fills its grid cell (`width: 100%`); the image holds ratio via `aspectRatio`.
Grid placement belongs to SFCC-80.

**Mobile/desktop boundary = 768px** (`breakpoints.md`, 48em) — the only confirmed foundation breakpoint between
the 402 and 1440 artboards, and where the grid already goes 4→8 columns. `min-width` is inclusive, so the 768
artboard gets the desktop card. Every hover rule is additionally gated on `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`
so a 768px touch tablet never gets hover-only content. See OQ-5.

**Hover is CSS-only, keyed on `:hover, :focus-within`.** No React hover state — 60 tiles re-rendering on pointer
move is a PLP perf defect. `:focus-within` is not optional: WCAG 2.2 AA requires the revealed size selector and
arrows be keyboard-reachable. All reveal selectors live in one place, the organism's recipe root part, selecting
descendants by the shared `data-card-slot` constants. Molecules stay hover-agnostic.

**One link per card (stretched-link).** The card holds a bag button, arrows, size options and a remove button —
nesting those in an `<a>` is invalid HTML and an a11y failure. The link wraps the product name only and carries
a `::after { position:absolute; inset:0 }` overlay; controls get `position:relative; z-index:1`. `href` arrives
pre-prefixed from the page. Uses `import {Link as RouteLink} from 'react-router-dom'` per `zimmColourSwatch` —
there is no `overrides/app/components/link/` override, contrary to a claim in `overrideStyling.md`.

**Reuse, don't rebuild:** `ZimmProductName`, `ZimmProductPrice`, `ZimmIcon` (`bag`, `close`, `chevron-left`,
`chevron-right` all exist in `ICON_MAP`). No new icons.

**VIC pricing is not a card concern** — precedence is the page mapper's job. Deferred to SFCC-778 (OQ-6).

## 4a. Arrows vs. indicator — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)

> *"position indicator is just for tablet and mobile, desktop hover is arrows"*

The two are **mutually exclusive**, not paired. Consequences for Steps 1 and 4:

**Split by pointer capability, not viewport width.** The gate is
`@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` — the same gate every other hover rule already uses:

- **hover-capable + fine pointer** → prev/next arrow buttons, revealed on `:hover, :focus-within`. No indicator.
- **everything else (touch tablet, mobile)** → `ZimmSlideIndicator`, always visible. No arrows.

Capability rather than width is what actually delivers the stated intent: the 768 artboard is a *touch* tablet,
and a width rule alone would give it arrows it can never hover to reveal. It also keeps this consistent with the
card's own hover rules rather than introducing a second, differently-keyed breakpoint. **Edge case, accepted:**
a desktop browser resized below 768 keeps arrows (it still has a fine pointer); a touch-screen laptop gets the
indicator. Both are the safe failure direction — nobody is shown a control they cannot operate.

**Two knock-on changes to the step pass criteria:**

1. **Step 1 — the indicator is NOT `aria-hidden` on touch.** The original criterion assumed the arrow buttons
   announce position, so the indicator could be hidden as duplicate. Where the indicator renders there are **no
   arrows**, so it becomes the only position signal — hiding it would be a 1.1.1 information loss. It needs an
   accessible position announcement (e.g. a visually-hidden "Image 3 of 8" live region, or `role="group"` with
   `aria-label`). Revised criterion: exposed and announced when it is the sole affordance.
2. **Step 4 — mobile image paging has no mechanism and no AC.** If the indicator shows position on touch, some
   touch gesture must change the image. No AC covers this; the ACs only describe desktop hover. See OQ-11.

## 4b. Touch image paging — RESOLVED (Marcel, 2026-09-02)

> *"scroll-snap it is"*

Native CSS scroll-snap. The dots remain a **passive readout**, visually unchanged from Figma — no enlargement,
no conversion to tap targets, so no departure from the design and no WCAG 2.5.8 problem to solve.

**Implementation shape: one scroll container on every breakpoint, not two mechanisms.**

The image strip is always a horizontally scrollable flex container with `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` and
`scrollSnapAlign: 'start'` on each slide. What differs by pointer capability is only the *affordance* layered
over it:

| | Mechanism | Affordance |
|---|---|---|
| hover + fine pointer | same scroll container | arrows call `scrollBy()`; no indicator |
| touch | same scroll container | native drag; indicator reflects position |

One container rather than two code paths means a single source of truth for "which image is showing", the
arrows become progressive enhancement over something that already works, and the desktop path inherits
keyboard scrollability for free.

**Active-index derivation:** prefer `IntersectionObserver` on the slides over a scroll listener — 60 tiles on a
PLP make a per-scroll-event listener a real perf cost, and the repo already has
`overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.ts` (**Tier 2 — import it, do not modify it**). The `scrollend`
event is an acceptable alternative. Left to the Implementer; either satisfies the pass criteria.

**Precedent:** the base `ProductScroller`
(`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller/index.jsx:79-84`) already uses
`scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'` with `overflowX: 'scroll'`. Same technique, already proven in this codebase.

**Accepted caveat:** swipe has no explicit affordance beyond the dots implying further content. This is the
universal mobile convention, and the alternative (enlarging 1px dots into 24×24 tap targets) trades an
invisible-but-expected gesture for a visible-but-off-design control. **Action: flag to Kiera that the mobile
gesture is undocumented in the design**, so it lands in the spec rather than being discovered in QA.

**Added Step 4 pass criteria:**
- The slide container carries `scrollSnapType: 'x mandatory'`; every slide carries `scrollSnapAlign`.
- Arrows are rendered only under `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`; the indicator only outside it; assert the
  two never coexist in the same DOM.
- Arrow activation moves the scroll position (assert `scrollBy`/`scrollTo` is called — jsdom does not lay out,
  so assert the call, not the resulting offset).
- The indicator's active index tracks the observed slide, and clamps at both ends.
- A single-image product renders no indicator, no arrows, and no horizontal overflow.
- No gesture library is added — `package.json` is untouched (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7).

# Upstream baseline

Tracks the current pinned version of `@salesforce/retail-react-app` and how far we have reviewed the upstream release stream.

<!-- upstream-release-tag: v10.0.0 -->

| | |
|---|---|
| **Current** | `10.0.0` (bumped 2026-05-18) |
| **Reviewed up to** | `10.0.0` |
| **Deferred** | none |

## Policy

See [.docs/upstreamPolicy.md](../upstreamPolicy.md). Bump opportunistically on security or relevant-SDK changes only.

## How to update this file

- After bumping: update **Current** and **Reviewed up to** together, and update the `<!-- upstream-release-tag: ... -->` marker so the watch workflow stops re-opening issues.
- After reviewing a release and deciding **not** to bump: update **Reviewed up to** only, and add a short note under **Deferred** explaining why (e.g. "v10.1.0 — UI-only template changes, no SDK impact").
- The `<!-- upstream-release-tag: ... -->` HTML comment is read by [.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml](../../.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml) — keep the exact format.
