content.content:
feat(ui-kits): add badge slot to ZimmProductCard (SFCC-236)

Adds the merchandiser badge (Figma "Tag" overlay) that SFCC-236's own
approved AC requires but the shipped card never rendered. The design was
believed not to exist, but is in fact present, unchanged, on every
Size/Type variant checked in the Figma component set — nested inside
"Image Group" (ZimmProductCardMedia's domain, not ZimmProductCardContent's,
where an earlier pass had looked for it).

- ZimmProductCardMedia: new optional `badge` prop, rendered top-left of the
  image using already-registered tokens (var(--zimm-scale-xl)/-l for
  position, textStyle="caption" + an explicit uppercase transform for the
  label, since the raw Figma text node carries none).
- ZimmProductCard: `badge` threaded through, gated by a new `showBadge`
  VARIATION_CONFIG column (shown on plp/wishlist, suppressed on home per
  Dani Rivett's scope note on the ticket).
- ZimmProductCardContent: corrected its own docblock, which previously
  claimed no design existed for the badge at all.

Also fixes a second issue found during the same Figma/AC/comment cross-
check: the hover image-swap to the model photo was unconditionally enabled
for every variation, including Home — but Dani's comment explicitly
excludes that hover behaviour from Home, and the AC that superseded it
three days later was never reconciled with that comment. Per the confirmed
comments > ACs > designs authority order, added `showHoverImageSwap` to
VARIATION_CONFIG (false for home) so Home no longer swaps to a supplied
hoverImage on hover. Home's own hoverRevealsPrice behaviour (a separate
mechanism) is unaffected.

Stories and Vitest coverage updated across all three components for both
changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---DF544AD---
docs(ui-kits): confirm badge is always a single value, not a list (SFCC-236)

A Figma Dev Mode Connect Note on the separate "Product Cards" file
(QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs, node 3448:35976 — distinct from the design-system
component-set file cited elsewhere in this docblock) confirms: "only 1
product badge will show up on these product cards - depending on the
configured hierarchy, the highest priority badge will be shown," with
that priority logic owned by SFCC-225.

Closes the open question flagged during the earlier Figma/AC/comment
audit — whether `badge?: string` might need to become an array to match
SFCC-225's already-merged backend, which writes `c_productBadges` as a
priority-sorted array. It doesn't: the array is exactly what feeds a
single value once a real mapper exists (`c_productBadges[0]?.productBadge`),
not a shape this prop itself needs to carry. No functional change — the
prop was already correctly shaped; this records the confirmation for
whoever writes that mapper.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---1C6F044---
fix(ui-kits): fix close-icon size and badge/close vertical alignment (SFCC-236)

Found during a live-browser visual audit — both were invisible to the
existing test suite, which checks DOM presence and text content, not
rendered geometry.

- Close icon rendered at 24x24 (Chakra's default), not Figma's specified
  16x16 (confirmed via the real "Close" node's three-level nesting:
  48px frame > 24px touchContainer > 16px Icon). Fixed with
  boxSize="var(--zimm-icon-size-md)", an existing, already-registered
  token that matches exactly.
- badge and close were centring their content within two different
  total heights (64px vs. close's fixed 48px), because badge relied on
  padding alone to size itself instead of a fixed height — padding grows
  the box to fit padding + content, it doesn't reproduce a frame's fixed
  size the way Figma's own "Tag" (also a fixed 48px, matching close
  exactly) does. Landed badge's text 9px below close's icon. Fixed by
  giving badge the same height: var(--zimm-scale-1200) (48px) close
  already uses, plus display:flex + alignItems:center to centre content
  within that fixed height rather than padding it outward.

Added a regression test asserting badge.height === close.height
directly, since geometry regressions like this have no other guard in
this suite.

fix(ui-kits): fix close-icon size and badge/close vertical alignment (SFCC-236)

Found during a live-browser visual audit — both were invisible to the
existing test suite, which checks DOM presence and text content, not
rendered geometry.

  16x16 (confirmed via the real "Close" node's three-level nesting:
  48px frame > 24px touchContainer > 16px Icon). Fixed with
  boxSize="var(--zimm-icon-size-md)", an existing, already-registered
  token that matches exactly.
- badge and close were centring their content within two different
  total heights (64px vs. close's fixed 48px), because badge relied on
  padding alone to size itself instead of a fixed height — padding grows
  the box to fit padding + content, it doesn't reproduce a frame's fixed
  size the way Figma's own "Tag" (also a fixed 48px, matching close
  exactly) does. Landed badge's text 9px below close's icon. Fixed by
  giving badge the same height: var(--zimm-scale-1200) (48px) close
  already uses, plus display:flex + alignItems:center to centre content
  within that fixed height rather than padding it outward.

Added a regression test asserting badge.height === close.height
directly, since geometry regressions like this have no other guard in
this suite.

+  image-swap had never respected Dani's comment excluding it, per this repo's confirmed

+  Note on the separate "Product Cards" file (`QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs`, node `3448:35976`): only

+  `c_productBadges` array feeds this single prop (`c_productBadges[0]?.productBadge`) once a real

+  text-content tests): `badge` sized itself via `paddingBlock` alone (64px) instead of matching
+  `close`'s fixed 48px, landing badge text 9px below the close icon. Fixed with an explicit
+  `height: var(--zimm-scale-1200)` + `display:flex; align-items:center`, plus a regression test
+  asserting `badge.height === close.height` directly.

+badge exists, not the interactive-vs-static question (SPR-16 vs. Figma's `touchContainer` +
+`State=Hover`) or which Badge component is authoritative (the card's own raw `Label` node vs.
+`40001471:20752`). The shipped `badge` is static text, no button, no hover rule — consistent with
+the "build it non-interactive per the requirement" call in §4c, not a new answer to it.

+above for the record of how the (also-wrong) removal was reached.

cd /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa
for i in $(seq 1 15); do
  if [ ! -d .git/rebase-merge ] && [ ! -d .git/rebase-apply ]; then
    echo "REBASE FINISHED (no rebase in progress)"
    break
  fi

  conflicts=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U)
  if [ -n "$conflicts" ]; then
    non_registry=$(echo "$conflicts" | grep -v "^\.claude/registry/" || true)
    if [ -n "$non_registry" ]; then
      echo "STOP: non-registry conflict found:"
      echo "$non_registry"
      break
    fi
    echo "Iteration $i: regenerating registry to resolve conflict in: $conflicts"
    node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs > /dev/null 2>&1
    git add .claude/registry/
  fi

  out=$(GIT_EDITOR=true git rebase --continue 2>&1)
  echo "$out" | tail -5
  echo "----"

  if echo "$out" | grep -qi "no rebase in progress\|is not possible because you have unmerged files\|error: could not apply"; then
    if echo "$out" | grep -qi "error: could not apply"; then
      continue
    fi
  fi
done
echo "=== FINAL STATE ==="
git status --short
git log --oneline -3

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNPostBuild

Marcel's own senior dev. Nothing built here — this skill judges what was built, writes what goes
public, and holds the conversation with CodeRabbit and the reviewer.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**Input:** `SFCC-236` — a Jira key. Reads three files under
`~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/`:

- **`handoff.md`** — Build's record: steps, commits, Scorer verdicts, rework rounds, gate numbers,
  UNIFORM findings, what went unverified
- **`plan.md`** — what was meant to be built
- **`findings.md`** — the gate table, with its 🟡 CLARIFY assumptions

If `handoff.md` is missing, Build either did not finish or ran before this was written. Say so and
reconstruct what you can from the branch's commits — but flag the audit as partial, because the
Scorer verdicts and UNIFORM findings are not recoverable from git.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get a five-agent sweep. Honour the scale the
plan chose. Nothing too crazy, no overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — audit against both artefacts

Two documents, two different questions. Neither is covered by the loop that just ran.

### `findings.md` — did the gate hold?

Walk every row. For each:

- **🔴 BLOCKED** — was it resolved before Build started, and by what?
- **🟡 CLARIFY** — this is the one that matters. Each of these carried a **stated assumption** into
  the plan. **Did that assumption actually hold once the code existed?** Nothing else in the chain
  revisits them. An assumption that turned out wrong mid-build, that nobody went back to, is the
  most likely thing to reach the PR unnoticed.
- **🔵 NOTE** — still true? A note that has become a defect is a finding.

### `plan.md` — did the build deliver?

- Every step shipped what it promised, with its Scorer verdict.
- The diff matches the file manifest. Anything in the diff that isn't in the manifest is a scope
  finding — even if it looks correct.
- Every file's tier is what the plan said it was.
- **Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.** Never a finding.

Use `zm-orchestrator` for the manifest-versus-diff conformance pass. It already does exactly this
judgement at step scope.

---

## Phase 2 — the whole-feature sweep

Per-step scoring is **structurally blind** to a pattern applied consistently but wrongly: it
passes every individual review. On this project a systematic spacing error survived five commits
and every score, and was only found afterwards. This phase exists for that.

Run it in two directions, internal first.

### Internal — does the feature agree with itself?

No external rubric. One question: is this internally consistent?

- Every recipe the same shape — same `parts` convention, same registration, same naming
- Every component the same structure — export, props type, story, test
- Every token used the same way for the same purpose
- The same value not typed twice in two places

A divergence here is a finding even when both variants are individually defensible.

### External — does that shared shape conform?

Only once you know what the feature's own pattern *is*:

- **The exemplar PR** — does the feature match what it established? Where the exemplar is itself
  inconsistent, say which variant this work followed and whether that was the better choice. Do
  not report a divergence from an unstable pattern as a defect.
- **`.claude/rules/*`** — do the rules hold across the whole feature, not just per file?
- **Figma, end to end** — the rendered feature against the named nodes, every variant and state.
  Remember the node-type discriminator and never cross-compare the two Figma files.

Use `zm-tester` for this, fanning out across the feature rather than one step. Every finding
carries **UNIFORM** or **ONE-OFF** — at this scope, UNIFORM is what you are hunting.

---

## Phase 3 — if the audit fails

**Hand back to `zimmerMANNBuild`. Do not fix it here.**

The auditor becoming the author is exactly the independence that makes this phase worth running,
and Build has a Scorer and a rework cap that this skill does not.

Report the defect with its evidence, return the work, and **re-audit when it comes back.** A
re-audit is a fresh pass, not a check that the named item changed.

---

## Phase 4 — the PR

Write the body yourself. Do not call `/pr-checklist` — its output is the team's format, and this
one is yours.

**The body describes the diff that actually shipped, not the plan.** If the two differ, the diff
wins and the difference is worth a line.

Include: what changed and why · the tier of every touched file, with any Tier 2 approver named ·
what was tested and the real numbers · anything deliberately deferred, with the owning ticket ·
anything left unverified.

**Never in a PR title, body, commit message or code comment:**
- Claude attribution of any kind — no `Co-Authored-By`, no mention
- CodeRabbit mentions
- A citation of any local-only doc. `~/Dev/fed-handbook.md` and its predecessors are Marcel's
  personal files. Where the same rule exists in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`, cite that.
- Draft or pending disclaimers

Match the house standard by reading Marcel's own previously authored PRs on this repo, not by
inferring a format.

---

## Phase 5 — write it down, then present

**First write `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md`:**

```
# PostBuild — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Head: <sha>   Audited: <date>

## Audit — findings.md
| # | Gate item | Severity | Held? | Evidence |
<one row per row of findings.md. For every 🟡 CLARIFY: did the assumption hold?>

## Audit — plan.md
| Step | Delivered? | Commit | Notes |
<plus: files in the diff that were not in the manifest>

## Sweep — internal consistency
<does the feature agree with itself — recipes, structure, token use>

## Sweep — external conformance
<exemplar PR · .claude/rules/* · Figma end to end>

## UNIFORM findings
<the ones a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## PR body as written
<the exact text>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>
```

**Then append a block per review round**, as the loop runs:

```
## Round <n> — <date>
Findings received: <n> (CodeRabbit <n>, reviewer <n>)
| # | Finding | Verdict | Fixed in | Reply posted? |
<VALID / INVALID / OUT OF SCOPE / DEFER, with the evidence for each decline>
```

This file is read by **`zimmerMANNBuild rework`** — so it knows what was already declined and why,
rather than re-litigating it — and by **`zimmerMANNDevImprover`**. Write it even when the audit is
clean; a clean audit that left no record is indistinguishable from one that never ran.

## Then present

Give him, in **"ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead"** register:

1. The diff summary — files, tiers, commits
2. The audit result — every gate item and plan step, with anything that failed
3. The sweep result — **UNIFORM findings first**, they are the point of this skill
4. The proposed PR title and body
5. What could not be verified

Then **stop.**

**On his go: push and open the PR.** Not before. Push is the first irreversible, outward-facing
step in the chain, and it is his to authorise.

---

## Phase 6 — the review loop

When CodeRabbit or a reviewer requests changes:

1. **Hand the findings to `zimmerMANNBuild rework`.** It verifies each finding is real before
   anything is touched — CodeRabbit has run as low as 1-in-6 correct on this repo — then fixes and
   commits the valid ones.

2. **Draft a reply for every finding when it comes back.** Every thread gets a written answer:
   - **Fixed** — what changed, and the commit
   - **Declined** — the specific quotable repo rule, doc, or empirical result that makes it wrong.
     Not an opinion.
   - **Deferred** — the owning ticket or the person who decides

   **A fix commit with no in-thread reply does not count.** A prior PR here carried 18 threads with
   zero human replies; the process was being followed on the PR before it and was dropped entirely.

3. **Show him the full batch, then post on his go.** One approval covers the set.

4. Repeat until approved. If CodeRabbit raises the same objection a third time, stop re-running it
   and answer the threads instead — it has nothing to learn from unanswered comments.

**Before final hand-off, re-run the manifest check — not just once, at the end.** Phase 2's
manifest-versus-diff audit is a snapshot, not a standing guarantee. Any fix round in this phase
(a CodeRabbit rework, a reviewer's requested change, or a gap Marcel spots and Build fixes
directly) can add a file outside the original manifest — including a legitimate, individually-
authorized Tier 1/2 exception. If it does, that file belongs in the plan's manifest and in
postbuild.md's own audit paragraph, not left for the audit to silently go stale. Before presenting
the final state for merge, confirm the manifest audit's claim still matches `git diff
<base>..HEAD --numstat` exactly — if it doesn't, append a dated correction (same pattern as
plan.md's own "Open questions" section) rather than leaving the original claim uncorrected.

---

## The owner rule — everywhere outward-facing

The audit report, the PR body, and every reply.

Every finding names **who resolves it**: Marcel, Tim, a designer, a BA, QA. A blocker owned by the
designer and one owned by Marcel need different actions.

**Where the owner is senior or lateral, phrase it as a question to them — never a directive.**
"Should this route via X, or have I misread it?" not "change this to X." Ask confirmatorily.

Before anything posts, count the asks. A review that mentions one person eight times reads as
hiding behind their authority.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write code.** Every fix goes back to Build. This skill audits, writes, and posts.
- **Never push or post without an explicit go.** Both are outward-facing and irreversible in
  practice.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never re-litigate a settled decision.** If the plan decided it and the build honoured it, it
  is not a finding — report a *mechanical consequence* of a decision, never the decision.
- **Say what you could not verify.** An audit that finds nothing has not been shown to be capable
  of finding anything.

Marcel is gathering node URLs. **Resume by pasting them against the table in

`40000223:2822` **`Product card / Product-card`** is a single component set, **20 variants**:

| Axis | Values |
|---|---|
| `Size` | Desktop (288w) · Mobile (179w) · Hero (288w) |
| `State` | Default · Hover |
| `Type` | Home · **PLP/PDP** · Wishlist · `Defualt` *(sic, Hero only)* |
| `Unavailable/coming soon` | False · True |

Maps onto the ACs cleanly. Figma merges PLP and PDP into one `Type`; SFCC-236's
"Recently Viewed Full History" variation states *"same behavior as PLP card"*, so it is
`Type=PLP/PDP` — **there is no fifth variant to design.**

The rail is `40000587:38471` **`Recently Viewed / Recently Viewed`**, 3 sizes:
Desktop **1440** (5 cards @288, exact fit) · Tablet **768** (3 @256 visible, 2 hidden) ·
Mobile **402** (2 @201 visible, 3 hidden).

### Blocker #3 — RESOLVED BY THE DESIGN. It is a bag icon.

`Card-content Size=Desktop` (`40002109:26906`) contains, at
`Content > Frame > Product name and attributes > Product name and icons > Icons > touchContainer`:

```
<instance id="40002109:26891" name="Icon_bag" x="4" y="4" width="16" height="16" />
```

documentation board but is **not placed inside any card variant**. Figma therefore agrees with
**SPR-14/SPR-15** (amended wishlist→cart) and **contradicts CRM-113–119**.

housekeeping — someone should strike the CRM rows so the next reader isn't misled.

reveals on hover — matching the AC exactly. `Attributes` (Colour + Size text) and `Price` and a
`Link` atom are all present in the shared Card-content, with per-`Type` visibility set on the instance.

Verified 04.72 (408944644) directly. Its ownership rule: *"Each component is owned by the earliest
epic in the sequence where it appears… if a product card component appears on PDP, PLP and Homepage,
all three variations must be designed and locked as part of the PDP."* **PDP's design scope lists
"product card"; PDP components-finalised = Aug 13 (Sprint 3), passed.** Search & Recommendations

homepage-template scope, not the card.

contradicts the same page's ownership rule. 🔴 → 🟡, wishlist variant only.

For finding 2, I'm thinking through Dani's scope note using a kitchen analogy: the manager said "no ketchup for Alice or Bob," but the note-taker only wrote down "no ketchup for Alice," accidentally truncating the instruction and leaving Bob unprotected. Technically, the instruction was to hide the badge and hover-swap behavior on both the Homepage card and the Recently-Viewed carousel, but only one of those two locations got the fix applied.

The Homepage got a real code switch that disables badge+hover-swap when the variation is set to 'home', but there's no equivalent switch for Recently-Viewed since that carousel is part of a future ticket (SFCC-83) that hasn't been built yet. content.text:
**Finding 1 — the missing shared file**

Picture the codebase as a house with several rooms. One room (`zimmProductCardMedia`) builds the little arrow buttons for flipping through product photos, and tags that chunk of markup with a label so other rooms can find it:

```tsx
<chakra.div __css={styles.carousel} data-card-slot="carousel">
```

`data-card-slot="carousel"` is just a name tag stuck on that HTML element — think of it like writing "KITCHEN" on a door.

A second room (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`, the styling rulebook) needs to say "when someone hovers over the card, make whatever's behind the door labelled KITCHEN fade in." So it has to write the same word, `"carousel"`, into its own rules — it can't just point at the first room's copy, it has to retype it.

A third place (the test files) also needs to check "did the thing labelled KITCHEN actually show up?" — so they type `"carousel"` too.

Right now, that word `"carousel"` is spelled out by hand in at least three separate places, plus a similar situation for one other value (a media-query string used for "does this device support hover"). Nothing links them together — they just happen to say the same thing today because whoever wrote them was careful. The only safety net is a comment that says, in effect, *"hey, if you ever rename this, remember to go update the other file too."* That's a sticky note, not a lock.

The plan for this build actually anticipated this exact problem and named a fix in advance: a small file called `zimmProductCardShared.ts` that would hold the real word once — `export const CAROUSEL = 'carousel'` — and every other file would `import` it instead of retyping it. That file was never created. So instead of one label everyone reads from, we have several people writing "KITCHEN" on separate scraps of paper from memory.

**Why it matters:** if someone later renames the door to `"gallery"` in the room that builds it, but only updates two of the three other places, nothing breaks loudly — no red squiggly line, no failing build. The styling rule just quietly stops finding its target, and the hover effect silently stops working, on every product card, everywhere, with no error to tell you why. That's the whole danger of copy-pasted "shared" values: they only stay in sync as long as everyone remembers, forever.

**Why it's cheap to fix:** nothing needs to be *decided* — the values already exist and already agree with each other today. It's purely a "cut these values out of three places, paste them into the one file the plan already named, have everyone import from there instead." No design judgment call, no risk of changing behaviour, just removing the trap.

---

**Finding 2 — the half-copied instruction**

Dani (a stakeholder on the design/product side) left one instruction with two parts, in a Jira comment:

> *"we don't want the hover action (model photo) on the homepage **or the recently viewed carousel**"*

The person building this card did the right thing and went looking for every place that instruction should apply. They found it, and wrote a comment directly in the code explaining the decision:

> *"Dani's comment also says 'we don't want the hover action (model photo) on the homepage,'"*

Read that quote again — it stops right there. It never says "...or the recently viewed carousel." The code then goes on to correctly turn the feature off for the Homepage case (there's a real setting, `showHoverImageSwap: false`, wired up for `variation: 'home'`). But there's no equivalent setting for "recently viewed," because that's not a thing this card knows how to be yet — it's a future ticket (SFCC-83) that hasn't been built.

Here's why that's a problem, not just a typo: the *only* two places this full, two-part instruction exists right now are (1) a Jira comment, and (2) a private planning document that lives outside this code repository entirely, on this machine. Neither of those will be open in front of whoever eventually builds SFCC-83. The only thing they'll actually look at is this component's code — and its own comment, in its own words, tells them the instruction was just about the homepage. So they'll do the obviously-reasonable thing: reuse the closest existing mode, `variation: 'plp'`, for their new "recently viewed" row of cards. But `'plp'` mode has the hover photo-swap *turned on* — the exact opposite of what Dani asked for the carousel. Nobody did anything wrong in that moment; they just inherited an incomplete note and had no way to know it was incomplete.

It's the difference between a decision being *made* and a decision *surviving*. This one was made correctly and then lost in transit.

**Why it's a one-line fix, not a build task:** we're not being asked to build the Recently Viewed carousel's suppression logic today — there's nothing to attach it to yet, since that variation doesn't exist. The fix is just to finish the sentence in the comment: add something like *"— the carousel half of this instruction has no code path yet; whoever builds SFCC-83 should not just reuse `variation: 'plp'` as-is."* That's it. It costs nothing and stops the same information loss from happening twice.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNBuild

The executor. Takes an approved plan and builds it, one step at a time, with every step tested,
scope-checked, scored and seen by Marcel before it becomes a commit.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.** A skill cannot pin the session model — the loop
agents are pinned to Sonnet in their own frontmatter regardless.

**Scale to the work.** A two-point story does not get the full loop. The plan states the scale it
chose and why; honour it. Over-scaled machinery is a defect, not thoroughness. Nothing too crazy,
no overthinking.

---

## Two modes

**`build`** — `SFCC-236 rework` is a Jira key. Reads `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/plan.md`
and executes it. This is the default.

**`rework`** — invoked as `rework <TICKET>` after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has
requested changes. Skips planning entirely; see the last section.

If no plan exists for the ticket, stop and say so. **Do not plan here** — that is
`zimmerMANNPreBuild`'s job, and building from an unplanned story is how an afternoon gets burned
on the wrong thing.

---

## Before the first step

1. Confirm the branch. **Not `develop`, not `main`** — a `PreToolUse` hook blocks every Write and
   Edit there. If the branch is wrong, stop.
2. Confirm the working tree is clean, or that everything dirty is expected and belongs to this
   story. Registry churn under `.claude/registry/*.md` is automatic and expected.
3. Read the plan's file manifest, tiers and per-step pass criteria. **Any file marked BLOCKED
   stops the run** until Marcel confirms owner approval.
4. Record the baseline: run the four per-step gates now and note the numbers. A gate that is
   non-zero at baseline is not a failure you introduced.

---

## The loop — once per step

```
Implementer  →  Tester  →  Orchestrator  →  Scorer  →  [Marcel]  →  commit
                   ↑                          │
                   └────── REWORK, max 3 ─────┘
```

**1. `zm-implementer`** builds the step. Only the files the step names. It never stages and never
commits.

**2. `zm-tester`** fans out its own angle sub-agents, re-pointed for this step, and reports
findings with CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE and UNIFORM/ONE-OFF labels, plus what it tried to falsify and
what it could not verify.

**3. `zm-orchestrator`** returns a scope verdict — IN SCOPE / UNDER / OVER / BLOCKED. Under and
over carry equal weight.

**4. `zm-scorer`** takes both and scores six axes. PASS or REWORK.

**REWORK returns to the Implementer with a specific instruction. Maximum three rounds.** On the
third, stop and surface to Marcel — three failures means the plan or the criteria are wrong, not
the implementation.

### Per-step gates — the cheap four

Run every step. Seconds each.

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test                        # includes recipeGuards, the hard styling gate
npm run lint                        # compare counts, not the exit code
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs    # new unacknowledged findings only
```

Two traps: `npm run lint` exits non-zero at a healthy baseline, so **compare the count against
your baseline and ignore the exit code**. And never append arguments to it — `pwa-kit-dev lint`
forwards `--`-args into `execSync`, which can silently turn the gate into a writer.

The plan's per-step pass criteria layer **on top of** these, they do not replace them.

### The visual checkpoint

**After any step that changes rendered output, the loop stops.** The plan marks which steps those
are; if it doesn't, assume any step touching a component, a recipe or a page does.

Tell Marcel exactly:
- the URL and the viewport to open
- the Figma node to compare against — the one for **that variant and state**
- what should be on screen
- what would indicate a defect, including anything that will look wrong but is correct

Then **wait.** Do not proceed on assumption. This is the only gate on this stack that catches a
layout defect — `width: 'xl'` passed every automated check and destroyed the global footer.

Until it has happened, the Scorer's Design fidelity axis is UNVERIFIED, not passed.

### The commit

**The skill commits, not an agent.** Only after: Scorer PASS, and the visual checkpoint passed if
one was owed.

One step, one commit. Conventional Commits — the `commit-msg` hook enforces it. **No Claude
attribution, no CodeRabbit mentions, no `Co-Authored-By` line.** Use Marcel's previously authored
commits on this repo as the reference for tone and body.

Then move to the next step.

---

## Before handing off

Once every step has passed, run the expensive gates **once**:

```
npm run build-storybook             # then run the interaction + a11y suite against it
npm run test:story                  # real BrowserStack, scoped to the Jira key
npm run test:max-file-size          # runs a full build
cr review --base develop            # CodeRabbit locally, full review before anything is public
```

Storybook needs a verified-free port and a build you can prove is yours — a stale server on 6006
produced a silently meaningless pass once. Check the served build matches your own before trusting
any result.

Then **write the handoff** to `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/handoff.md`:

```
# Handoff — <TICKET>
Branch: <branch>   Base: <sha>   Head: <sha>

## Steps
| # | What | Commit | Scorer verdict | Rework rounds |

## Gates (real numbers, not claims)
| Gate | Result | Baseline |

## UNIFORM findings
<each one, with file:line — these are what a per-step review structurally cannot catch>

## Could not verify
<named, with why>

## Outstanding
<anything left, or "none">
```

**Write it even when everything passed.** PostBuild reads this file, and it may run in a different
session — a handoff that exists only in conversation does not survive the session ending.

Then present the same content to Marcel and **hand off to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`. This skill does
not push and does not open a PR.**

---

## Rework mode

Entered after a PR is open and CodeRabbit or a reviewer has requested changes.

**Read `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/postbuild.md` first.** It records what earlier rounds
already declined and why. A finding that was declined with evidence in round one does not get
re-litigated in round three — check before you verify anything, and if you disagree with a previous
decline, say so rather than silently reversing it.

**1. Verify every finding before touching anything.** CodeRabbit has been wrong on this repo
often — one batch ran 1-in-6 correct. Treat each finding as a hypothesis, not a fact. Per finding:

- **VALID** — reproduce it, cite `file:line`, fix it
- **INVALID** — say what is actually true, with the evidence, and draft the reply
- **OUT OF SCOPE** — real but not this story's problem; name the owning ticket or the person
- **DEFER** — real, in scope, but blocked on a decision; name who decides

**2. Fix only the VALID ones.** Same rules as build mode — the Implementer touches only what the
finding names, never stages, never commits.

**3. Re-run the cheap four**, plus the visual checkpoint if the fix changes rendered output.

**4. Commit the fixes here**, same rule as build mode — the skill commits, never an agent. Reference
the review thread each commit answers.

**5. Hand back to `zimmerMANNPostBuild`** with: what was fixed and in which commit, what was
declined and why, and the evidence behind each decline. **PostBuild owns the push and the
in-thread replies** — every finding gets a written answer, including the declined ones.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never push. Never open or update a PR.** That boundary belongs to PostBuild, which presents
  first and pushes only once Marcel has given the go.
- **Never write to the repo's config** — `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CODEOWNERS`,
  `.docs/memory/**`, `.docs/prd/**`. Tier 1 Governance.
- **Never touch a Tier 1 file** without Marcel naming it and confirming owner approval.
- **Never expand scope.** Something worth doing that the plan didn't ask for gets reported, not
  done. Report it and let Marcel decide.
- **Local-only docs are never citable** in a commit message or a code comment. Cite `AGENTS.md`
  or `.claude/rules/*` instead.
- **Say what you could not verify.** Silence reads as "nothing wrong" when it may mean
  "didn't look there".

/**
 * Shared DOM-contract constants for the ZimmProductCard organism and its composed molecules
 * (ZimmProductCardMedia, ZimmProductCardContent) — defined once here so every producer (the JSX
 * that stamps a `data-card-slot` attribute) and consumer (the organism's own recipe selectors,
 * plus this component family's test suites) reads the same value instead of each independently
 * retyping it. Same pattern, smaller scale, as `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`.
 */

/**
 * The ten `data-card-slot` attribute values that wire the organism's hover/reveal CSS
 * (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) to specific descendant DOM nodes. `media` / `badge` / `close` /
 * `carousel` / `indicator` are stamped by `ZimmProductCardMedia`; `content` / `bag` / `price` /
 * `sizeChips` / `notifyMe` by `ZimmProductCardContent`. Do not rename a value here without
 * checking both molecules' own docblocks, which document what each slot is for.
 */
export const CARD_SLOT = {
  media: 'media',
  badge: 'badge',
  close: 'close',
  carousel: 'carousel',
  indicator: 'indicator',
  content: 'content',
  bag: 'bag',
  price: 'price',
  sizeChips: 'sizeChips',
  notifyMe: 'notifyMe',
} as const;

/**
 * Hover-capable-pointer gate shared by every hover-only affordance across the card family
 * (desktop arrows, the hover-reveal price/size-selector swap, the notify-me reveal) — the
 * resolved SFCC-236 decision that arrows and the touch slide-indicator are mutually exclusive by
 * pointer capability, not viewport width.
 */
export const HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY = '@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)';

No deletions, no renames detected by git across the `origin/develop..HEAD` boundary (the shared-file relocation happened entirely within this branch's own history, so it collapses to a plain `A` at the final path — confirmed separately via `git log -p ... | grep rename`, which shows `d2fe7a7` created it at `organisms/zimmProductCard/zimmProductCardShared.ts` and `0f35e0c` renamed it to `ui-kits/zimmProductCardShared.ts`).

## 2. Manifest conformance — Modified files

| File | Plan says | Diff shows | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` | Tier 2, planned | Append-only: 6 imports + 6 registry entries, nothing else touched (`git diff` confirmed directly) | Matches plan exactly |

| `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts` (+3/-1) | Tier 2, disclosed mid-build | Same correction mirrored | Real, but see CODEOWNERS gap below |

## 3. A claim in my own task framing does not hold up — checked, not assumed

I was told plan.md "now includes two dated corrections: a mid-build Tier 1/Tier 2 disclosure, and a note that `zimmProductCardShared.ts` was relocated from inside the organism's folder to directly under `ui-kits/`." I read the file in full and grepped it directly:

```
grep -n "relocat" plan.md          → no matches
grep -n "zimmProductCardShared" plan.md → lines 96, 103, 491 only
```

Only **one** of the two claimed corrections is actually present (the Tier 1/Tier 2 disclosure at plan.md:67-84). **The relocation note does not exist anywhere in plan.md.** Line 104 still reads "it stays co-located (precedent: `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`)" — i.e., the plan's own text still describes the file as living beside its one owning component, which is where `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts` actually lives (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`, confirmed via `find`). I'm flagging this because a message describing the plan's own contents is not a substitute for reading the plan — this is exactly the kind of thing this role exists to catch independently, per my instructions. It has no tier/owner consequence (CODEOWNERS routes the whole `ui-kits/` tree, old or new location, to `pwa-squad-a` + `pwa-squad-b` — verified below), so it's a documentation gap, not a scope violation on its own.

My hunch is this is a controlled-component pattern problem — the component likely relies on a `selectedValue` prop to render the selected chip, and `onSelect` just calls back without the Storybook story wiring that callback to update the arg, so the click fires but nothing ever changes the prop feeding the visual state.

Actually the actions addon alone just logs calls — it doesn't automatically feed back into args, so the story likely needs `useArgs()` from `@storybook/preview-api` or a stateful wrapper to actually update `selectedValue` when `onSelect` fires. Since the user wants to understand the "why" behind this, I should check the actual story file for `ZimmSizeChipGroup` (and possibly the organism story) to see exactly how `onSelect`/`selectedValue` is wired before diagnosing further.

This confirms it: none of these stories wire up an `onSelect` handler explicitly, yet the user reports actions being logged, so I need to check whether `meta` sets `argTypes` for `onSelect` to trigger Storybook's automatic action logging.

Actually, Storybook's actions addon typically auto-detects `on*`-prefixed props via an `argTypesRegex` config and auto-mocks any unhandled ones with a logging function — that's almost certainly what's happening here since no real `onSelect` is passed in args. But since `selectedValue` in these stories is just a static string with no accompanying state update, clicking a chip fires the auto-logged action without actually changing the visible selection.

This isn't a bug in `ZimmSizeChipGroup` itself — it's behaving correctly as a controlled component that reports intended changes via `onSelect` without managing its own state, consistent with the codebase's container/presentational pattern. The real gap is that only `KeyboardNavigation`, with its custom stateful `render`, actually demonstrates live click-to-select interaction; the other four stories are static snapshots rather than interactive demos.

Only `KeyboardNavigation` wires a local state hook back into `onSelect`, so clicking a chip there actually updates the visual selection — the other stories just fire the auto-mocked action with no feedback loop. If Marcel wants more stories to be live-interactive, the fix is either converting `Default` to that same stateful-wrapper pattern, or using Storybook's `useArgs()` hook inside a render function for a more idiomatic CSF3 solution.

The clearest response here is to diagnose the root cause precisely — controlled component plus non-stateful story args plus Storybook's default action-mocking — clarify the component itself isn't broken, then ask Marcel whether they want to leave things as-is or make more stories interactive via a stateful wrapper.

## Round 5 — 2026-09-04 (live-bug fix, found by Marcel in Storybook, not by an audit pass)

Marcel found this hands-on, not through a planned audit step: clicking a size chip logged the
Storybook action but never visually selected. Root cause: `ZimmSizeChipGroup`/`ZimmProductCard`
are correctly controlled components, but every story except one passed a static `selectedValue`
with no handler wired to update it — a stories-wiring gap, not a component defect.

Five commits: made the `Default` story of both `ZimmSizeChipGroup` and `ZimmProductCard`
interactive first, then — on Marcel's explicit "I want all instances to work" — extended it to
every remaining story that renders enabled, clickable chips: `PLPOutOfStock`, `Wishlist`,
`WishlistOutOfStock`, `SingleImage`, `MultipleImages`, all 8 PLP/Wishlist `nodeCoverage` stories,
`ZimmSizeChipGroup`'s `WithSelection`/`WithDisabledSize`, and `ZimmProductCardContent`'s
`WithSizeChips` — 16 stories total. Extracted the repeated wrapper into `productCardFixtures.ts`
as `LiveSizeSelectionCard` rather than tripling it, and caught+fixed a regression the extraction
itself introduced (always starting unselected, which would have silently dropped `Wishlist`'s
deliberately pre-selected chip).

**Explicitly not touched, with reasons recorded at the time:** `Home`/`HomeOutOfStock` and their
`nodeCoverage` counterparts (no size-chip slot exists for Home), `OneSize` (a static label, not a
radiogroup), the atom-level `zimmSizeChip` stories (a single isolated chip has nothing to select
between), `ZimmProductCardContent`'s `Default`/`WithAttributes`/`Unavailable`/`LoadingPrice` (all
inherit `showSizeChips: false`). `PLPOutOfStock`/`WishlistOutOfStock`'s chips are now wired but
invisible either way — the picker is CSS-hidden whenever a card is unavailable, with no counter-
rule to reveal it; flagged to Marcel as a possible separate gap, not fixed here.

**Marcel separately asked whether keyboard nav (arrow keys, Enter/Space) also worked** — verified
yes, by design: the component's own `selectIndex` function is the single call site both the click
handler and the arrow-key handler use, so lifting `onSelect` to real state (this round's whole
fix) covers keyboard for free. His live report that arrow-key nav wasn't visibly selecting turned
out, on investigation, to be this session's own browser-automation tool failing to deliver a
synthetic keydown into Storybook's nested preview iframe — confirmed by dispatching a real
`KeyboardEvent` directly on the focused element, which worked exactly as coded (focus and
selection moved together, atomically). Not yet root-caused on Marcel's own side; he said LGTM
without confirming which of the follow-up questions explained it.

**Gates:** `tsc` clean · `test` 873/873 · `audit:tokens` 1 pre-existing finding outside this diff,
same as every prior round.

4	type ZimmSizeChipStyleProps = {
5	  selected?: boolean;
6	  disabled?: boolean;
7	};
8	
9	/**
10	 * Border colour precedence: disabled > selected > default — same "no state stacking" shape as
11	 * zimmTextInput.css.ts's resolveBorderColour. Default and Disabled both resolve to
12	 * 'transparent' rather than a real colour: Figma's Default/Disabled variants (nodes
13	 * 40003038:125875 / :125873) render as plain text with no box at all, so the always-present
14	 * `border` shorthand on `chip` below is made invisible rather than removed outright — the same
15	 * "transparent border avoids a layout shift" idiom zimmColourSwatch.css.ts's `swatch` part
16	 * uses for its own unselected state.
17	 */
18	export const resolveBorderColour = ({ selected, disabled }: ZimmSizeChipStyleProps): string => {
19	  if (disabled) return 'transparent'; // Figma Disabled (…125873): no box, muted text only
20	  if (selected) return 'var(--zimm-color-border-focus)'; // Figma Selected (…125874): outline-only box
21	  return 'transparent'; // Figma Default (…125875): no box, plain text
22	};
23	
24	/**
25	 * Background is transparent in every branch: Figma's Selected variant (…125874) is an
26	 * outline-only box — border present, no fill — so no state here ever paints a background.
27	 * Kept as an explicit disabled/selected/default cascade, matching the other two resolvers'
28	 * shape, rather than collapsed to a bare `'transparent'` return, so a future Figma revision
29	 * that does introduce a fill only has to change one branch's value.
30	 */
31	export const resolveBackgroundColour = ({ selected, disabled }: ZimmSizeChipStyleProps): string => {
32	  if (disabled) return 'transparent';
33	  if (selected) return 'transparent'; // outline-only box — was var(--zimm-color-bg-05); Figma has no fill
34	  return 'transparent';
35	};
36	
37	/**
38	 * Text colour precedence: disabled > selected > default. Selected does NOT get an inverted
39	 * (white) treatment — Figma's Selected variant (…125874) keeps the same dark default text
40	 * colour as Default and only adds the outline box via resolveBorderColour above.
41	 */
42	export const resolveTextColour = ({ selected, disabled }: ZimmSizeChipStyleProps): string => {
43	  if (disabled) return 'var(--zimm-color-text-muted)';
44	  if (selected) return 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)'; // no inversion — outline-only box, not filled
45	  return 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)';
46	};
47	
48	/**
49	 * Recipe for the PDP size chip atom — a single 28x28 (--zimm-scale-700) size option, read
50	 * directly off the size-chip Figma component set (node 40003038:125876) for this exact
51	 * component's dimensions and state list. Four Figma-defined states — Default / Selected /
52	 * Focus / Disabled — resolved by the three `resolveXxxColour` helpers above and the
53	 * `_focusVisible` block below. Hover and Active/pressed are NOT part of that variant set, so
54	 * neither is implemented here — same "don't invent an unspecified visual state" precedent as
55	 * zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts's `pageButton` part.
56	 *
57	 * The STRUCTURE of all four states is directly confirmed against individual Figma PNG exports
58	 * of each variant (Default …125875, Selected …125874, Disabled …125873, Focus …130506) — not
59	 * inferred: Default and Disabled render as plain text with no border/box at all; Selected is
60	 * an outline-only box (border present, no fill — text stays the normal default colour rather
61	 * than inverting); Focus is Selected's border box plus an additional outer ring (confirmed by
62	 * its 34x34 Figma frame vs. 28x28 for the other three — the ring extends past the chip
63	 * itself). Only the exact border/text COLOUR TOKEN choice (`--zimm-color-border-focus` /
64	 * `--zimm-color-text-default` / `--zimm-color-text-muted`) remains this file's own inference
65	 * from precedent rather than a pixel-confirmed hex breakdown — flag for UI-designer
66	 * confirmation if a token choice doesn't match.

69	  parts: ['chip'],
70	  baseStyle: (props: ZimmSizeChipStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
71	    chip: {

content.thinking:
Marcel's raising a valid point—these fixture files sit flat at the root of ui-kits/, which normally only holds atoms/, molecules/, and organisms/ subfolders, so having them as siblings there breaks the established pattern.  Given the theme of this whole conversation, where quick decisions keep needing revisiting, I should actually verify the current directory structure and honestly consider whether a dedicated subfolder would be the better convention rather than defending the flat placement by default.

I'm also noticing a real scalability concern: if this "loose file in ui-kits root" approach becomes precedent, future features needing shared molecule/organism code would each dump more loose files there, cluttering the root over time. A grouping folder feels like it could avoid that mess as the codebase grows.

Breaking that invariant is worth reconsidering. I should check whether there's a more idiomatic location — maybe a neutral, explicitly-named "shared" folder at the ui-kits level rather than nesting under a single organism, or look for precedent elsewhere in the app for this kind of cross-component shared type.

I recall AGENTS.md establishes that shared types across components already have a designated place outside component folders, split into commerce, components, and hooks files — but that's specifically for types, not constants or fixtures. Since there's no perfect precedent for shared runtime constants across sibling components within ui-kits, I want to check the actual directory listing to gauge how disruptive introducing a new subfolder would be before presenting Marcel with a considered recommendation.

Marcel wants a more fundamental justification for why these files sit outside the atomic-design hierarchy at all, not just where they should go. I need to reason from first principles about why something like a shared product-card type would need to live outside atoms/molecules/organisms in the first place.

The core issue: the organism (`ZimmProductCard`) needs to apply hover CSS that targets DOM nodes rendered deep inside its child molecules — like hiding a price element when hovered to reveal a size picker. Since these are separate components, the mechanism is a shared contract: child molecules stamp `data-card-slot` attributes on their DOM nodes, and the organism's recipe selects against those same attribute values. Both producer and consumer sides need to agree on the exact string values, which is exactly why this needs to live in a shared file rather than inside any single component.

But that approach doesn't actually work for hover-reveal across siblings, since Media and Content aren't parent/child but sibling subtrees under the organism — CSS `:hover` only naturally cascades to descendants, not siblings. That's precisely why the shared selector vocabulary lives at the organism level: it's the only common ancestor that can see both siblings' DOM and wire the cross-sibling CSS, which is why both need matching `data-card-slot` values for the organism to select into.

Also, the project's own documented architecture (verified in plan.md) explicitly rejected a React-state-based hover approach for performance reasons — 60 tiles re-rendering on pointer move would be a real PLP perf regression — confirming the CSS-attribute-selector pattern is a deliberate decision, not an oversight, and it's what necessitates this shared vocabulary.

That reasoning gives a solid answer to "why do these files exist out here": they let sibling molecules select into each other's DOM via shared attribute values, and that cross-component vocabulary can't belong to any single atom/molecule/organism without recreating the backward-import problem already caught and fixed twice this session. content.text:
Good push — let me separate the two, because they don't have the same justification.

**`zimmProductCardShared.ts` (`CARD_SLOT`/`HOVER_CAPABLE_QUERY`) has a real structural reason to exist outside any single component.** The organism's recipe needs to write CSS selectors that reach into DOM its *sibling* molecules render (`ZimmProductCardMedia`, `ZimmProductCardContent`) — e.g. "on card hover, hide the price Content renders, reveal the size-chips Content renders." That's not incidental: the plan explicitly chose CSS-only hover with no React hover state, specifically because 60 tiles re-rendering on every pointer move on a PLP grid would be a real perf regression. Given that choice, the organism *has* to select into sibling DOM by a shared attribute vocabulary — there's no component that could "own" that vocabulary without creating exactly the backward-import problem already fixed twice. Duplicating those values has a real, silent-failure risk (a mismatched string just stops a CSS rule from ever matching, no error anywhere).

**`productCardFixtures.ts` doesn't have that justification, and I should have caught this before extracting it.** It's pure Storybook/test sample data — a couple of demo images and a size array — with zero production coupling. The "problem" it solved was a few `.stories.tsx` files typing the same mock image twice. That's not a drift risk the way the DOM-contract constants are: two stories showing slightly different sample data breaks nothing, it's just cosmetic. Storybook fixtures being duplicated per-file is normal, low-stakes, and arguably fine as-is — I don't think this ever needed to become a shared file at all.

So the honest answer: one of these earns being "out here" on real architectural grounds; the other probably shouldn't exist as a separate file in the first place. Want me to un-extract `productCardFixtures.ts` back into each story file, and leave `zimmProductCardShared.ts` as the one genuine exception at `ui-kits/` root?

All clean. Here's what I actually checked, live in Storybook — not just re-running `tsc`/tests:

**`ZimmSizeChipGroup`/`ZimmSizeChip`** (the component with the real logic change):
- Click and arrow-key navigation both correctly move `aria-checked`/`tabIndex` together, atomically, confirmed via direct DOM inspection after each action.
- Disabled-skip verified: from a pre-selected chip, ArrowLeft correctly jumped over a disabled sibling to the next enabled one.
- `OneSize` correctly renders a plain `<span>`, no role, nothing focusable.
- Atom states (Selected/Disabled) carry the right `role="radio"`/`aria-checked`/`disabled`/`tabIndex` combination in isolation.
- Visual: the selected box moves correctly on both click and keyboard nav (confirmed the very thing you first flagged as broken).

**`ZimmSlideIndicator`** (token fix): now sits under "Elements" in the sidebar, confirmed visually. Computed colors are byte-identical to before the fix — active `rgb(25,25,25)`, inactive `rgb(209,209,209)` — zero visual regression, `role="group"` with `aria-label="Image 1 of 5"`, never `aria-hidden`.

**`ZimmProductCard` organism** (relocations + citation removal + un-extraction + interactivity): `Default` renders image/name/badge/price correctly, exactly one real link (`/product/123`), size-chip click works. `Wishlist` loads with `M` correctly pre-selected — the regression I caught earlier holds fixed. The remove button has a real, descriptive `aria-label`.

**`nodeCoverage`**: spot-checked `Wishlist_Desktop_Default` — its own independently-duplicated interactive wrapper works correctly (seeded at M, click-to-L works), confirming the accepted duplication didn't diverge.

**`ZimmProductCardMedia`/`ZimmProductCardContent`**: both render correctly post-un-extraction; Content's `WithSizeChips` click-to-select confirmed working too.

**Gates, fresh:** `tsc` clean, 873/873 tests passing.

**Honest gap:** I verified the accessibility *tree* directly (roles, names, states, live regions) — that's what any screen reader, including VoiceOver, actually reads from. I did not run actual VoiceOver and listen to its output; I have no tool that captures speech. If you want that literal check, it'd need to be you, on the Mac, with VoiceOver on (Cmd+F5) — I'm confident based on the tree that it would announce correctly (radiogroup "Select a size", each option as "XS, radio button", checked state changes), but I can't claim to have heard it.
